## Goal

Make the ship skill's release version-bump step work for Python projects, so a
repo with only `pyproject.toml` (no `package.json`) can be released through the
canonical `run-release.js` / `scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` pipeline.

## Context (discovered during the TTS v0.1.1 release, 2026-10-25)

`bump-version.js` hard-requires `package.json`:

```
Version bump failed. Check that package.json has a valid version field and node is available.
```

and the merge script's version-bump block only stages `package.json`
(`git add package.json`). Consequence: the canonical release cannot run for
Python-only repos (e.g. `/home/rgardler/projects/tts` — this session had to use
the manual direct-merge fallback). The downstream steps already tolerate the
absence of `package.json`/`CHANGELOG.md` (non-fatal), so this is the sole
hard blocker for Python projects.

## Version-source convention

`bump-version.js` resolves the version source by convention:
`package.json` (repo root) when present, else `pyproject.toml` `[project].version`.
When neither exists/declares a version, exit non-zero with a combined, actionable
error message. `merge-dev-to-main.sh` stages whichever file was bumped
(`package.json`, or `pyproject.toml` for Python-only repos).

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `bump-version.js` resolves the version source by convention — `package.json` when present, else `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` — and fails with a clear, combined error message when neither declares a version.
- AC2: `--bump patch|minor|major` increments `[project].version` in place in `pyproject.toml`, touching no other part of the file (comments, key order and all other fields byte-identical).
- AC3: Existing `package.json` behaviour is unchanged; the JS regression suite's `bump-version` tests still pass (they already cover patch/minor/major + validation errors).
- AC4: New tests cover: pyproject patch/minor/major bumps; legacy `[tool.poetry]`-style version (if supported) or `version = "dynamic"` / missing version → non-zero exit with an actionable message; invalid semver → non-zero and file unmodified (no partial writes).
- AC5: `merge-dev-to-main.sh` stages the bumped file generically (`git add pyproject.toml` when no `package.json` exists) and the version-bump step no longer aborts a Python-only repo; tag/changelog/derived-file steps behave as before (changelog/derived-file absence already non-fatal).
- AC6: Ship skill docs updated (`ship/SKILL.md` + `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`) to state the package.json-or-pyproject.toml version-source convention.

## Implementation notes

- **Test-first order**: write/extend tests before implementation (AC3 regression
  suite + AC4 new tests), then `bump-version.js`, then `merge-dev-to-main.sh`,
  then docs (AC6).
- **pyproject.toml edit approach**: line-based, section-aware rewrite of just the
  `version = "…"` line inside the `[project]` table (handle single/double quotes),
  preserving all other bytes — no TOML parser dependency (Node has no built-in
  TOML module). `--dry-run` must not write.
- **`[tool.poetry]`/`version = "dynamic"`**: deferred (not supported in this
  slice) — a repo with only a poetry-style/dynamic/missing version exits non-zero
  with a message naming the candidate sections and explaining why (open question,
  see plan comment).
- **Verification**: `generate-changelog.js` reads commit history (not
  package.json), so a Python repo's changelog step should work once the bump
  passes — verify end-to-end with a Python-only fixture repo during the
  changed-scope test gate.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js`
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`
- `tests/node/test-bump-version.mjs`
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md`
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`

## Out of scope / related observations

- The `gh pr create` step requires a GitHub remote; local-bare-origin repos
  still cannot complete a PR-based release even with this fix. Consider a
  follow-up item if local-first repos should get an automated direct-merge
  path.
- `generate-changelog.js` reads commit history, not package.json, so Python
  repos get changelogs for free once the merge script gets past the bump — verify during implementation.
data.title: ship: bump-version.js must support Python projects (pyproject.toml version source)

# implement.py finish: concurrent sessions orphan each other's commits via the shared local-dev fast-forward

> **Provenance:** mirrored from `LP-0MVN8XWPY009AEXO` (llm worklog,
> deleted after this item was created). `discovered-from:LP-0MVN8XWPY009AEXO`.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` rewrites the **shared** main-checkout `dev` ref (pre-push
`git merge --ff-only <child commit>`, then a post-push parent sync) while
pushing the same commit to `origin/dev`. The ref mutation and the push are not
atomic, not locked, and not verified, so two sessions finishing different
children of the same epic can interleave: a commit that was fast-forwarded into
local `dev` but not (yet) pushed becomes invisible to `origin/dev`, and the next
`finish` run either moves local `dev` past it or silently skips the whole
pre-push fast-forward, leaving the commit reachable only from its feature
branch. `finish` never checks that the commit it pushed is actually an ancestor
of the new `dev` tip, so it reports success while the commit is orphaned.

## Users

- **Agent (implementation session)** — needs `finish` to either publish its
  commit on `dev` or fail loudly naming the hash; never to report success for a
  commit that did not land.
- **Agent (parent/epic driver)** — needs the shared local `dev` to remain a
  trustworthy base, so the next child worktree is not forked from a stale or
  orphan-pinned ref.
- **Producer / operator** — needs no manual `git merge --no-ff <orphan>`
  recovery, and needs to be able to tell from the work item whether the work
  actually reached `dev`.

Example user stories:

> As an implementation agent, when a transient network error aborts my push, I
> want `finish` to leave `dev` and the remote in a consistent state so my retry
> cannot silently publish a different commit and drop mine.

> As an epic driver, I want a per-repository in-flight `finish` lock (or
> equivalent detection) so two children implemented concurrently cannot
> interleave ref updates in the shared checkout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — local-dev sync is remote-verified.** The pre- and post-push local
  `dev` updates only fast-forward to a commit that is already on
  `origin/dev` (or refuse loudly, naming the ref/hash, when local `dev` has
  moved since the worktree base). Local `dev` is never left pointing at an
  unpushed `finish` commit after a failed push.
- **AC2 — ancestry assertion.** After the push, `finish` asserts its own commit
  (including any rebased replacement hash) is an ancestor of the pushed
  `origin/dev` tip (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> refs/remotes/origin/dev`)
  and fails loudly, naming the commit hash, when it is not.
- **AC3 — concurrent `finish` runs are serialised or detected.** Concurrent
  `finish` runs in one repository either block on a per-repository in-flight
  lock or fail fast with an actionable message; a lock left by a crashed
  process must not deadlock the repository.
- **AC4 — regression coverage.** A test drives a failed first push followed by
  a second commit made from the older base and asserts the first commit stays
  reachable from `dev` (hermetic bare-remote + clone sandbox, following the
  existing `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` and
  `tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py` patterns).
- **AC5 — documentation.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (post-push local parent
  sync section) and any affected `docs/dev/` pages describe the new lock and
  ancestry-verification behaviour, including the recovery path when a `finish`
  refuses.
- **AC6 — full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **The source of truth is the SorraAgents framework repo**, not this project:
  the code is `SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`. The installed
  runtime copy at `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` is a real copy refreshed by
  `SorraAgents/scripts/install_pi.sh`, so a source fix only takes effect after
  reinstall. This item is tracked in the SorraAgents worklog (mirrored from the `llm`
  discovery record `LP-0MVN8XWPY009AEXO`, since deleted); the code change
  must land in SorraAgents `dev`.
- **Do not remove the rationale for the pre-push fast-forward** without
  replacing it: it exists so the pre-push context-budget gate measures the main
  checkout with the new files present (commits touching `AGENTS.md` etc. would
  otherwise be rejected by a stale checkout). Any redesign must preserve that
  property or wire the gate to the worktree tree instead.
- **Preserve the safe-skip semantics** of `_sync_parent_branch`
  (SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1 AC2): never force-update, never `reset --hard` the
  shared checkout, never lose local commits, never fail a finish that already
  pushed.
- **No force-push and no rewriting of `origin/dev`.** Recovery must remain
  additive (rebase own branch, or merge).
- **Locks must be crash-safe**: `fcntl.flock`-based (kernel-released on process
  death) following `SorraAgents/skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`; no PID or
  timestamp bookkeeping. A stale lock file must not block a later `finish`.
- **Test hermeticity**: tests must use their own bare remote + clone under
  `tmp_path` and must never mutate the live checkout's refs.
- Agent test runs go through the test skill (`run_tests.py`); the full suite is
  enforced at the dev-push gate.

## Existing state

- `phase_finish` Step 5 (pre-push, `implement.py` ≈ L4273–4340): fetch
  `origin/dev`, `git checkout dev`, `git merge --ff-only origin/dev`, then
  `git merge --ff-only <commit_hash>`. Any failure raises into a broad
  `except Exception` that only logs "push will proceed from the stale
  checkout" — the fast-forward is all-or-nothing and silently disabled
  whenever local `dev` has moved.
- Step 6 pushes `<branch>:refs/heads/dev` (`git_push_to_dev` ≈ L1457). A
  generic (e.g. network) failure returns `False` → `RuntimeError` → work item
  reset to `open`; a timeout raises `PushTimeoutError`; a non-fast-forward
  raises `PushNonFastForwardError` handled by `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`
  (≈ L3905), which rebases in the worktree and retries.
- Step 8 (`_sync_parent_branch`, ≈ L1952) fast-forwards local `dev` to
  `refs/remotes/origin/<parent>`; it safe-skips on dirty/diverged/fetch-failure.
- `phase_start` Step 6.5 uses the same helper before `git worktree add`, so a
  local `dev` pinned at an unpushed commit is silently used as the base for
  every subsequent child worktree.
- No per-repository lock exists anywhere in `implement.py` (grep for
  `flock` / `.lock` returns nothing), and there is no post-push ancestry
  assertion.
- Observed incident (2026-10-25): commit `25e99ff8`
  (LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7) was orphaned while `b0b69053` → `0c34c7d8`
  (LP-0MVN4L7UX003KGTI) landed; `git reflog dev` shows the local `dev` fast
  forwards to `0c34c7d8` at 02:45:53 and no entry for `25e99ff8` until the
  manual merge `f847a971` at 02:55:23 (`git merge --no-ff 25e99ff8`).

## Desired change

1. Make the pre-push fast-forward **verified and reversible**: only advance
   local `dev` to a commit whose objects are confirmed on `origin/dev` (e.g.
   push the branch first and sync afterwards, or fast-forward local `dev` from
   the remote-tracking ref and *verify* the child commit is an ancestor before
   moving), and on push failure restore local `dev` to
   `refs/remotes/origin/dev` instead of leaving it on the unpushed commit.
2. Add a post-push ancestry assertion (AC2) that names the offending hash and
   leaves recoverable state (worktree + branch retained, work item not
   advanced).
3. Add a per-repository `finish` lock (AC3) guarding the whole
   commit → fast-forward → push → sync window, with a bounded wait and an
   actionable timeout message.
4. Keep non-fast-forward recovery behaviour intact, extended to verify
   ancestry after the retry push.
5. Cover all of the above with hermetic regression tests plus a doc update.

## Key Files

- `SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` Step 5
  (pre-push fast-forward) and Step 6/8 (push + `_sync_parent_branch`): needs
  verified/reversible local-dev sync, the ancestry assertion, and the
  per-repository lock.
- `SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev` /
  `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`: needs to surface the pushed tip and verify
  ancestry after a rebase retry.
- `SorraAgents/skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — reference implementation of
  crash-safe `fcntl.flock` locking to reuse (or a small sibling
  `repo_lock` helper).
- `SorraAgents/tests/test_implement_finish_concurrent_orphan.py` — new
  regression suite for AC1–AC4.
- `SorraAgents/tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py` — extend the
  existing sandbox helpers; AC1/AC2 assertions on the pre-push fast-forward.
- `SorraAgents/tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` — extend to
  assert ancestry after the recovery rebase.
- `SorraAgents/skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document the lock, the verified sync
  and the refusal/recovery path.
- `SorraAgents/scripts/install_pi.sh` — reinstall step so the fixed skill copy
  is active for subsequent sessions (no code change expected).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** all `finish` sessions for a repository run on the same host
  and share one filesystem, so an `fcntl.flock` mutex is sufficient (no
  cross-host locking needed). If that ever changes, the lock becomes advisory
  and the ancestry assertion (AC2) is the remaining safety net.
- **Assumption:** `origin/dev` is the only publication path (membership of
  `main` is the ship skill's job), so verifying ancestry against
  `refs/remotes/origin/dev` is a complete success criterion.
- **Risk (regression):** removing or reordering the pre-push fast-forward can
  re-break the pre-push context-budget gate for commits that touch `AGENTS.md`
  and friends. Mitigation: keep the property explicitly under test (extend
  `tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py`/`test_implement_push_*`)
  rather than relying on the current implementation detail.
- **Risk (contention):** a repository-wide lock serialises `finish` windows;
  with the full suite deferred to the push gate the window is short, but a
  long pre-push hook still serialises siblings. Mitigation: bounded wait with
  a clear timeout message pointing at the holder, never an indefinite hang.
- **Risk (stale lock):** a crashed holder must not block the repo forever.
  `flock` is released by the kernel on process death, so a lock *file* may
  remain harmlessly on disk — tests must assert a leftover file does not block
  the next run.
- **Risk (scope creep):** fixing the false-negative push result
  (`SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX`) and the test-cache identity issue
  (`SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L`) are adjacent but separate; they stay linked work
  items, not scope of this change.
- **Risk (diagnosis uncertainty):** the exact 2026-10-25 interleaving is not
  fully reconstructable from the reflog; the ACs are therefore invariants
  (verified sync, ancestry assertion, lock) rather than a single narrow fix.

## Related work

All items below live in this (SorraAgents) store. This item was mirrored from
`LP-0MVN8XWPY009AEXO` in the `llm` worklog — the incident was observed while
implementing `llm` children, but the defect is agent infrastructure in this
repository. That discovery item was deleted once this mirror was synced.

- `LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7` — the orphaned child (cold-prefill budget enforcement);
  recovered by merge `f847a971`.
- `LP-0MVN4L7UX003KGTI`, `LP-0MVN4L7KT003XUBA` — siblings that landed while the
  orphan was in flight.
- `SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1` (completed) — "implement.py finish leaves local dev
  behind after pushing to remote dev"; introduced the post-push
  `_sync_parent_branch` this item hardens.
- `SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX` (open) — "finish reports 'git push to dev failed' when
  the push actually landed": the mirror-image failure (false negative) that
  makes an orphan indistinguishable from success.
- `SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG` (open) — run_tests live-repo guard flags concurrent
  origin ref updates / push timeout: same concurrency surface.
- `SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L` (open) — test-cache key ignores worktree identity, so
  post-push verification can cache-serve (relevant to any post-push assertion).
- `WL-0MLG0DSFT09AKPTK` (completed) — "Process-level mutex for import/export/sync":
  precedent for a crash-safe lock in this toolchain.
- `SA-0MV8311B3005DNG8` (completed) — live-repo test guard false-positives on
  concurrent agent `dev` fast-forwards: same concurrency surface in the test
  harness.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (agent → producer):** "The implementation lives in the SorraAgents framework
  repo (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`), while the incident was observed
  from the `llm` worklog. Should the fix be implemented directly under the LP
  item, or should a mirrored `SA-…` work item be created in the SorraAgents
  store to carry the code change, with the LP item as the discovery record?"
  **Recommended:** create a mirrored `SA-…` item in the SorraAgents store —
  `implement.py start` creates a worktree from the *current* repository, so an
  LP item cannot satisfy the worktree-isolation contract when the code lives in
  SorraAgents.
  — **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "This should be in ../SorraAgents,
  recreate there, wl sync and delete this item." Final accepted answer: this
  item (`SA-…`, SorraAgents store) carries the fix; the `llm` item
  `LP-0MVN8XWPY009AEXO` was deleted after the mirror was synced.
  Source: interactive producer reply (2026-10-25); prior answer: none.
  Research: repository layout inspection (`SorraAgents/skill/implement`,
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement` real-copy install, `scripts/install_pi.sh`).
- **Q (agent, resolved by repo evidence):** "Is the vulnerable code still
  present, or has it already been fixed?" — **Answer:** still present. The
  installed runtime copy is byte-identical to the SorraAgents source; Step 5
  still fast-forwards local `dev` to the unpushed child commit, no per-repo
  lock exists (`flock`/`.lock` absent from `implement.py`), and no post-push
  ancestry assertion exists. Evidence: `diff`
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` vs
  `SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (identical);
  `grep -n "flock|\.lock"` (no matches).
- **Q (agent, resolved by repo evidence):** "Does the local-dev mutation
  actually leave an unpushed ref behind after a failed push?" — **Answer:** the
  observable evidence is consistent with it: `git reflog dev` in the `llm`
  checkout shows a fast-forward to `0c34c7d8` at 02:45:53, no local `dev`
  update for `25e99ff8` after its 02:46:53 commit, and a manual merge
  `f847a971` only at 02:55:23. The precise interleaving of the two sessions is
  not fully reconstructable from the reflog, which is why AC1–AC4 are written
  as invariants (verified sync, ancestry assertion, lock, regression test)
  rather than as a single narrowly-diagnosed code change.

# Prevent duplicate drive child sessions (one exclusive lock per child work item)

Migrated from ContextHub `WL-0MVNSNNLF004VPDB` (deleted after handoff). Discovered during
`WL-0MVLIHY1P002WP0D` (extraction of downtime-worker idle/poller modules), 2026-10-25.

## Problem statement

Two concurrent `implement.py drive <parent>` invocations can each spawn a child Pi session for
the **same** child work item in the **same** worktree, so two agents write the same files
simultaneously. Nothing serialises `drive`/`parent`/`start` invocations, and a child claimed by
another live process is indistinguishable from one that this process may resume.

## Users and user stories

- **Operator / downtime dispatcher** (runs `implement.py drive <epic>` — sometimes twice, from two
  panes or a retried cron slot):
  - As an operator, I want the second driver to refuse a child that is already held, naming the
    holder, so my in-flight child session is never corrupted.
  - As an operator recovering from a crashed driver, I want a stale holder to be reclaimed
    automatically with a logged warning, so I never have to hand-delete lock files.
- **Driven child session** (fresh Pi session implementing one child):
  - As a child session, I want exclusive ownership of my worktree for the life of my session, so
    my edits and untracked files are never overwritten by a sibling driver.

## Observed incident (evidence)

Two `implement.py drive WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7` processes (PIDs 1176064 and 1176470, started
11:52:41 and 11:52:50) each spawned a child session for the same child (`WL-0MVLIHY1P002WP0D`) in
the same worktree (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MVLIHY1P002WP0D-…`). Both wrote
`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` and the two new module files concurrently:

- one session's extraction overwrote the other's, briefly leaving a corrupt monolith (an interface
  truncated mid-declaration);
- untracked new files (`downtime-worker.idle.ts`, `downtime-worker.poller.ts`) were silently
  replaced, destroying in-progress work;
- the later session's `implement.py finish` removed the worktree under the still-running first
  session (its shell `cwd` vanished).

Sessions: A `01a172e8-0d51-702c-a5b2-db348fcc8d19` (11:52:52), B
`01a172e8-23b6-7448-87dc-3361db99a633` (11:52:58).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Mutual exclusion.** Two concurrent `implement.py drive <parent>` (or `parent`, or a manual `start <child>`) invocations for one child never both enter the child's critical section: the winner proceeds, the loser reports the child as held (`action: "skipped-held"`, with `held_by: {agent, pid, session_id, started_at}`) and performs **no** worktree creation or removal, **no** status/assignee mutation and **no** file writes.
2. **Lock primitive.** Exclusion is a non-blocking `fcntl.flock` on `<worklog>/locks/child-<work-item-id>.lock`, acquired in `phase_start` **before** the work-item claim and any worktree creation/resume, and held for the holder's lifetime. The lock file records owner metadata (agent, pid, session id, started-at, token).
3. **Release semantics.** The lock is released on normal exit, on exception/abort, and on SIGINT/SIGTERM (handler or `finally`); `SIGKILL`/crash release is guaranteed by the kernel. If the recorded owner pid is dead at acquisition time, the lock is reclaimed and a warning naming the reclaimed holder is logged (and surfaced in the report).
4. **Driver re-entrancy.** The driver's own subprocess chain and the driven child session it spawns (which runs `start`/`finish` for the same child id) are not falsely blocked: ownership is propagated by an explicit token (`IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN`, matching the token in the lock file) — never by "same pid" heuristics alone.
5. **Regression test.** A subprocess-level test runs two `phase_start`/`drive` invocations for one child concurrently and asserts: exactly one acquires, the other returns a held/skip report naming the holder, no worktree is created by the skipped one, and no file content differs from the winner's writes. Unit tests cover acquire/release, SIGTERM release, and stale-dead-pid reclamation with warning.
6. **Scope discipline.** Existing guards are preserved and not weakened: `skip-in-progress` classification, `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE` recursion refusal, the worktree placement guard, and the stranded-child finalisation ownership check.
7. **Documentation.** The behaviour, lock path, env token and failure messages are documented in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` and the `drive` section of `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, including how an operator diagnoses a held child.

## Constraints

- No new third-party dependencies (stdlib `fcntl` only); no polling/`sleep` loops.
- No wall-clock TTL that can expire under a legitimately long child session — the kernel lock is
  authoritative, and the recorded pid only serves stale-holder diagnostics and reclamation logging.
- Lock files live under the **worklog store** (`<worklog>/locks/`), never inside the worktree
  (a worktree can be removed mid-flight).
- The lock must not interfere with the host-wide `process_semaphore` slot pools, nor nest into them.
- Fail closed: ambiguity must produce a skip-with-report, never a second concurrent writer.

## Existing state

- `phase_start` (claim at ~L3883) claims the work item unconditionally — it never checks whether
  another live process already owns the item or its worktree.
- `_classify_child` (~L819) maps a non-terminal child to `skip-in-progress`; `phase_parent`
  (~L5256) treats "in_progress + worktree present" as resumable by this process, which is exactly
  the ambiguity that produced the incident.
- `_finalise_stranded_child` (~L5957) already performs an assignee-ownership check — a precedent for
  ownership-aware guards, but assignee is a human-visible hold, not a live-process signal.
- Reusable primitives exist: `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` (fcntl slot locks, kernel-released)
  and `skill/shared/queue.py` (`_DirectoryLock`).
- No lock directory or lock helper exists for per-work-item ownership today.

## Desired change

1. Add a small per-work-item lock helper (predicted new module `skill/shared/work_item_lock.py`)
   modelled on `process_semaphore`: non-blocking `flock`, owner metadata + token in the lock file,
   dead-pid reclamation with a logged warning, context-manager release on exception/signal.
2. Acquire it in `phase_start` as the first step after validation, wrapping claim + worktree
   create/resume; propagate the token to spawned driver/child processes via the environment.
3. Classify a held child as `skipped-held` in `phase_parent`/`drive` reports, with holder identity,
   and stop cleanly instead of starting a second session.
4. Cover it with the subprocess-level concurrency regression test plus unit tests, and document it.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/work_item_lock.py` — new: flock-based per-work-item lock (acquire, owner metadata,
  token ownership, stale-pid reclamation warning, context manager).
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — acquire the lock in `phase_start`; propagate the token in
  `_child_session_env`/`_invoke_implement`; new `skipped-held` classification and report fields in
  `_classify_child`/`phase_parent`/`phase_drive`.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_lock.py` — new: subprocess-level two-holder regression test.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_work_item_lock.py` — new: acquire/release, SIGTERM, stale-pid reclamation.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — new section: child lock, token, held-child diagnosis.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — `drive`/`parent` section: one child = one holder; what "held" means.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Re-entrancy is the main correctness risk.** The driver, its `parent`/`start` subprocesses and the
  driven child session all act on the same child id. Assumption: an explicit token in the lock file
  (plus a token in the child env) is the only ownership signal; pid equality is insufficient and
  "same session" heuristics are forbidden.
- **Signal handling risk.** A `SIGTERM` between claim and worktree creation must not leave a claimed
  item with no worktree; the handler must release and, where sane, revert the claim (mirroring
  `abort` semantics) or leave a comment for the operator.
- **False-positive risk.** A lock that outlives a killed-but-reclaimed pid must not block forever;
  the dead-pid check must be tested with a recorded pid that cannot be ours.
- **Human-visible hold vs live lock.** The producer sentinel `--assignee Map` is a *scheduling hold*,
  not a process lock; the two must stay distinct in reports so operators are not misled.
- **Scope creep (recorded, not in scope):** serialising whole `drive` invocations (a driver-level
  mutex) is a plausible follow-on but is not required by these ACs; file it separately if wanted.
- **Assumption:** only the implement skill needs changing; the downtime dispatcher's own
  coordination is out of scope.

## Related work

- `WL-0MVLIHY1P002WP0D` (ContextHub, completed) — the extraction that was corrupted mid-flight.
- `SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN` — drive timeout reconciliation (completed): retry path this guard must not break.
- `SA-0MVLJWRVO000QQNP` / `SA-0MVLJWTGP005XJPP` — stranded-child detection and safe finalisation
  (completed): ownership checks to stay consistent with.
- `SA-0MVLIZ33M009C5QY` — drive livelock on repeated `finishing_failed` (open): adjacent retry logic.
- `SA-0MVLKHY27005UK40` — drive each epic child in an interactive Herdr pane (open): spawns sessions
  through the same path, so it must honour the lock.
- `SA-0MUY9PSRS003V5CM` — driven child must work inside its worktree (`cwd` is not enough)
  (completed): the placement guard to preserve.
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`, `skill/shared/queue.py` — lock patterns to reuse.
- `SA-0MUV4C6RZ006GN5Z` / `SA-0MV0IWQJK0018O8D` (completed) — PriorityQueue directory-lock contention and its cross-process timeout test: directly relevant precedent for flock-based contention handling.
- `SA-0MVLJXTYY005XQDV` (blocked) — reconcile terminal child once the finish bound is exhausted: adjacent retry/reconciliation logic.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- Q: "Where does the fix land / which item owns it?" — Answer (operator): "Create a work item in the SA store, `wl sync`, and delete this ContextHub item once the handoff is complete." Source: interactive reply. Decision: this item (`SA-0MVOABYW00004978`) was created in the SorraAgents store with the full incident evidence; ContextHub `WL-0MVNSNNLF004VPDB` was deleted after the handoff.
- Q: "Guard mechanism (AC2)?" — Answer (operator): "A" — `fcntl.flock`-based per-child lock file under `<worklog>/locks/`, owner metadata recorded, dead-pid reclaimed with a logged warning. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Loser behaviour and guard breadth?" — Answer (operator): "A" — fail fast: the loser reports `held-by <agent>@<pid>` and skips the child (no waiting); the guard is enforced inside `phase_start` so `drive`, `parent` and manual `start` share one choke point. Source: interactive reply.
- Q (assumption, no answer yet): lock files live under the worklog store (never inside the worktree) so they survive worktree removal — recorded as a Constraint above.

## Plan (2026-10-27, session herdr-1793062619-1640855-2062)

Decomposed into five test-first child slices (effort Small, risk High — planning required):

1. `SA-0MVQ5A8WC0096BDL` — Test: per-work-item lock unit tests (task, root)
2. `SA-0MVQ5AE7L005M0NR` — Implement: shared per-work-item flock lock (feature, blocked by 1)
3. `SA-0MVQ5AI56001QXA4` — Test: subprocess two-holder concurrency regression (task)
4. `SA-0MVQ5AXLF002PAQ3` — Implement: acquire lock in phase_start + skipped-held (feature, blocked by 2 and 3)
5. `SA-0MVQ7VMRL00498YB` — Document child lock and held-child diagnosis (docs, blocked by 4)

Dependency order: 1 → 2 → {3} → 4 → 5. Test slices precede the implementation slices that satisfy them.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-27 03:47Z — planning session created 5 children (2 test, 2 feature, 1 docs), wired 4 dependency edges, added this plan block. No duplicates found; two candidate search hits (queue lock contention SA-0MUV4C6RZ006GN5Z, cross-process timeout test SA-0MV0IWQJK0018O8D) are precedent/reusable, not duplicates.

### Goal

Add `_pane_session_spawner` next to `_default_session_spawner` and select the
transport per invocation: pane driving only when Herdr is detected **and** the
operator opted in; otherwise the existing headless `pi -p` spawner is used
unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Pane-per-child in the caller's tab.** For each startable child, drive runs `pane split` with `--cwd` (no tab create), then `agent prompt`; asserted by a fake-CLI test.
- **Opt-in with fail-open fallback.** Pane driving activates only when `HERDR_ENV=1`, a resolvable herdr binary and `--pane-sessions`/`IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_PANE_SESSIONS=1` agree; tests cover absent and opt-in.
- **Environment isolation is preserved for pane children.** The child process receives `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1` and `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH` without `PI_SESSION_ID`/`PI_SESSION_FILE`; `pane split --env` args are asserted.
- **Focus behaviour.** Default is `--no-focus` so the caller's focus is unchanged; `--focus` switches to each new child pane and the flag passed to `pane split` is asserted.
- `_pane_session_spawner` returns the `_default_session_spawner` result shape plus `pane_id` and `transport`, so existing `phase_drive` success handling is unchanged.
- **Build, tests, and full suite.** Changed-scope tests pass before commit; the dev-push full-suite gate is green.

## Implementation notes

- `_pane_session_spawner(child_id, worktree_path, timeout, env,
  verbose=False)` → `{"success", "returncode", "reason", "pane_id",
  "transport"}`.
- Selection: `spawner = spawn_session or _select_session_spawner(...)`,
  keeping the existing `spawn_session` test-injection point. Detect with
  `HERDR_ENV=1` plus herdr-binary resolution (reuse the shared resolver);
  opt in via `--pane-sessions` or `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_PANE_SESSIONS=1`.
- New argparse flags: `--pane-sessions` / `--no-pane-sessions` (default:
  env-driven) and `--focus` / `--no-focus` (default `--no-focus`), threaded
  into `phase_drive`.
- Child env comes from the existing `_child_session_env`; the pane transport
  passes it as `pane split --env` pairs, and the TUI launch uses an
  `env -u PI_SESSION_ID -u PI_SESSION_FILE` prefix so the driving session's
  identity never leaks into the pane.
- Do **not** change `_default_session_spawner`: headless `pi -p` stays the
  default outside Herdr for the downtime worker, audit dispatch and CI.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py`
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (Step 6.1)

- Env-isolation and focus handling.
- Unit tests: detection matrix (herdr-absent / opt-out / opt-in), split/start/

- Doc updates for the flag, env var, focus default and headless fallback.

### Goal

Drive the pane-side lifecycle to completion in `phase_drive`: wait on session
state (never process exit), report blocked children, bound the wait with the
existing timeouts, and close or explicitly retain every pane — with additive
report parity for human and `--json` output.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Driver waits on session state, not process exit.** Completion of a child is decided by `agent wait --until done|blocked` plus the `phase_parent` stage re-read; tests cover done, blocked, timeout.
- **Blocked children are reported, not silently abandoned.** When an agent reports `blocked`, drive stops, records `blocked_child`/`blocked_pane`, leaves the pane open and names it.
- **No orphaned sessions:** a pane created by drive is either (a) closed once its child reaches a terminal stage or (b) retained and reported; tests assert close per success and no close when blocked.
- **Timeouts and iteration bounds are enforced across the new transport.** `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_CHILD_TIMEOUT` and `--max-child-sessions` still bound the wait; a timeout closes the pane and stops the chain.
- **Report parity.** Human and `--json` reports keep the existing shape and gain `pane_id` per driven child plus `transport`; the summary lists retained panes, asserted by tests.
- **Build, tests, and full suite.** Changed-scope tests pass before commit; the dev-push full-suite gate is green.

## Implementation notes

- `phase_parent` stays the authority for terminality; the `agent wait` result
  is only a fast-path/stop signal. Reuse `_reconcile_spawn_failure` so a child
  that reached a terminal stage before the wait expired is still reported as
  `completed-late`, not failed.
- `blocked` → report keys `blocked_child` / `blocked_pane`, a `retained_panes`
  entry, and an actionable message naming the pane (e.g.
  `herdr pane read <pane_id>`); title the pane via
  `herdr_pane.update_pane_title(status, pane_id=...)` (`⚠️`/`🚫` verdicts).
- Close path: `pane close <id>` after the child's terminal stage is confirmed;
  retain on blocked/failed with a verdict title. Never leak silently.
- `_emit_phase_report` gains additive keys only; the human rendering appends a
  "panes retained for inspection" list. Existing deterministic orchestration
  tests (`ScriptedParent` / `RecordingSpawner`) keep passing unchanged.
- Timeout behaviour keeps today's semantics: close the pane, record `reason`,
  stop the chain (reconciled against the child's real stage first).

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`phase_drive`, `_emit_phase_report`)
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py`
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (Step 6.1)

## Dependencies

- Pane session spawner and opt-in transport selection.

## Deliverables

- done / blocked / timeout lifecycle handling with `phase_parent` authority.
- Close-or-retain rule with pane-title verdicts.
- Report fields (`pane_id`, `transport`, blocked/retained panes) plus human
  rendering, with parity tests.
- Doc updates for blocked-child handling and retained panes.

data.description:
## Goal

Replace the whole-directory `node_modules` symlink in `implement.py start` with a **worktree-local link farm** so workspace packages resolve to the worktree's own source tree. Parent: SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO.

## Problem (parent: SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO)

`_ensure_node_modules_symlink` (~L1695 in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`) symlinks `<worktree>/node_modules -> <main-checkout>/node_modules`. When the main checkout's `node_modules/@worklog/shared` is a relative symlink `../../packages/shared`, every `@worklog/shared` import in the worktree resolves to the **main checkout's** `packages/shared/dist` (gitignored, built by `npm run build` in whichever checkout ran it last) — the worktree's own `packages/shared/src/**` changes are invisible to the build/test gate (false red, false green).

## Desired change (producer-decided: link farm)

Replace `_ensure_node_modules_symlink` with an idempotent link-farm creator:

- Create a **real** `<worktree>/node_modules` directory containing one symlink per main-checkout `node_modules` entry, recursing into scoped packages (`@worklog/*`, `@types/*`, …), and linking `.bin` as a whole directory.
- Override workspace packages (e.g. `@worklog/shared`) to the worktree's own `packages/*` — resolved relative to the worktree via the `workspaces` field or a small allow-list; keep the mechanism workspace-aware, not hard-coded to `@worklog/shared`.
- Keep `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks` (OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT) unchanged and working.
- Add a resolution check: `@worklog/shared`'s resolved package root must equal `<worktree>/packages/shared`; expose it in the `start` JSON report.
- Idempotent and refreshable: re-running re-materialises entries when the main checkout's dependency set changes. Documented refresh = re-run of the link step (or `implement.py start`) from the main checkout.
- No writes through the farm into the main checkout's `node_modules`/`dist`; `npm install` inside a worktree stays forbidden (AC5); automated `rsync` of worktree `dist` into the main checkout is rejected.
- Best-effort/non-fatal on tooling edge cases (Windows junctions per ContextHub `link-shared.mjs` precedent); degrade to the old whole-dir symlink behaviour for repos without a workspace shared package.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `implement.py start` outputs a real-directory link farm at `<worktree>/node_modules` (per-entry symlinks, scoped recursion, `.bin` whole-link) instead of a whole-directory symlink, with `@worklog/shared` resolving (`os.path.realpath`) to `<worktree>/packages/shared`.
2. The `start` JSON report includes the resolution-check result key (e.g. `shared_resolution_ok: true`, with the resolved root), present on both fresh `start` and refresh.
3. The step is idempotent (re-run creates no duplicates) and refreshable when the main checkout's dependency set changes; verified by automated tests from the F1 test-first item.
4. No writes pass through the farm into the main checkout's `node_modules`; the main checkout stays git-clean of everything except gitignored build artefacts after start → build → gate → finish.

## Goal

Produce a **valid clean-room measurement** of a single-item audit on the healthy Local Proxy and record it in `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md`, so the committed ≤ 10 min (600 s total LLM wall clock) gate has either a green result or an honest per-call shortfall profile that names the dominant call.

Parent: SA-0MVKXNWRS005EKBM. Prior evidence: SA-0MVI6VVC00029XO4 (4419.8 s) and SA-0MVJ3Q662006RDJR (1538.68 s / 3 calls, **not** clean-room — the slot query failed so the ceiling fell back to `--max-concurrency 2`).

This is the **verification-first (test-first) slice** of the parent: no runner behaviour change. If this lane meets the gate, the Lane B / Lane C siblings are closed as not-needed with this evidence.

## Validity preconditions (a run that fails these is INVALID, not evidence)

- `GET /llama/local/status` on the proxy reports `available_slots > 0`; the run's launch log must show a slot-query-derived ceiling (not `source=env` fallback).
- No concurrent audit run and no other `pi` session consuming the 2 proxy slots — coordinate an idle window with the operator.
- Target item has no children and 1–5 ACs (same shape as `SA-0MVI3608M0080QLW`, used by both prior measurements).
- An INVALID run is recorded **as invalid** with the failure reason and retried; it is never presented as gate evidence (the honesty rule from the 2026-10-23 record).

## Work

1. Verify the proxy is healthy and idle; capture the slot-status output verbatim into the run record.
2. Run the audit with the established command shape:
   `python3 skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py issue <small-item-id> --do-not-persist --force --json --green-run HEAD --debug-log /tmp/audit_after_<id>`
3. Extract the per-call `Per-call timing:` lines and the `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY` from the debug log; compute the total LLM wall clock.
4. Commit the run's timing lines as a fixture and add a test that re-derives the figures with the committed harness (`python3 scripts/measure_audit_performance.py --root <fixture-dir> --json`) and asserts that the per-call table, total and MET/NOT MET verdict recorded in the baseline doc match the parsed values, where the verdict is derived as `total <= 600 s`. No figure and no verdict may be hand-copied.
5. Record the measurement in `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` (re-measurement section + timeline entry): command, commit, model served, slot-query status and ceiling source, per-call table, total, gate verdict, and end-to-end wall clock as secondary context.
6. Comment the outcome on the parent: MET → Lane B / Lane C closed as not-needed; NOT MET → name the dominant call and hand the profile to Lane B.

## Test-first ordering

Step 4 (the doc/fixture consistency test) may be written against the fixture as soon as the run's debug log exists, before the doc table is finalised — the doc is then written to satisfy the test, not the other way round.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A clean-room run of a small single-item audit is recorded, with the proxy slot status showing `available_slots > 0`, a slot-query-derived ceiling, no concurrent audit/`pi` session, and the run record committed to `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` (command, commit, model served, slot-query status, ceiling source, per-call table, total). An INVALID run is recorded as invalid with its reason instead of being counted.
- A test parses the committed run fixture via `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py --json` and asserts that the per-call elapsed values, the total LLM wall clock and the MET/NOT MET verdict recorded in the baseline doc match the parsed values (`verdict == (total <= 600 s)`), so the evidence is asserted against harness output rather than hand-copied.
- The measured result — pass or the recorded shortfall with its lever decision — is committed to `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` including the command, model served, slot-query status and per-call profile, and the ≤ 10 min gate/regression-gate definition is left unchanged (Lane A passing requires no runner change).
- The end-to-end wall clock is recorded as secondary context alongside the total LLM wall clock, and the gate metric question is flagged for producer confirmation rather than silently redefined (parent OPEN QUESTION: total LLM wall clock assumed).
- The outcome is commented on the parent SA-0MVKXNWRS005EKBM: either MET (and Lane B/C closed as not-needed, with this item's evidence cited) or NOT MET with the dominant call identified and its duration, handing the profile to the Lane B child.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Read-only on the runner: no behaviour, timeout or verdict-semantics change in this item.
- Measurement only on the local proxy (remote fast models stay out of scope for the parent unless the producer authorises them).
- Do not launch the audit while another audit or `pi` session holds the proxy slots; if no idle window can be obtained, leave the item blocked with the environment reason rather than recording an invalid run as evidence.

# Verdict-provenance and cache-contract tests

## Target outcome

Specify, test-first, the verdict-provenance contract the gate must satisfy:
every gate verdict records which tree it ran against (worktree path + git
fingerprint) and whether it came from cache; a cached verdict is acceptable
only when its fingerprint equals the would-be-commit tree's; a clean change set
still causes exactly one suite execution (no duplicate runs); an identical tree
may reuse a cache hit.

## Definition of done

- Report-shape tests assert per-attempt keys: tree (worktree path),
  `git_fingerprint` (tree SHA), `cached` bool, and cache entry metadata
  (command / completed_at / scope) when served from cache.
- Cache-semantics tests: a stored entry whose fingerprint differs from the
  expected would-be-commit fingerprint is a miss (suite re-runs); a legacy entry
  lacking provenance metadata is a miss (fail closed); a matching fingerprint
  within TTL is a hit.
- Single-execution test: a clean change set through the gate runs the suite
  exactly once (no duplicate run after the provenance fields land).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The gate report records tree path, git fingerprint and the `cached` flag, with entry metadata (command / completed_at / scope) for cached verdicts.
- [ ] Foreign, stale or legacy (provenance-less) fingerprint entries miss and force a fresh run.
- [ ] **Existing green runs unaffected:** a clean change set passes exactly as today with a single gate suite execution (no duplicate run) — asserted by counting suite spawns.
- [ ] An identical tree with a matching fingerprint inside the TTL reuses the cache (no spawn).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_provenance.py` (new)
- `tests/test_test_cache.py` (fingerprint/cache assertions)
- `skill/test_cache.py` (`lookup`/`run_cached` contract under test)

## Deliverables

- Contract tests defining the report and cache semantics; they pass once F7/F8 land.

## Dependencies

- **SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 child F3** (env pass-through predicate).

# Abort invariants for the finish gate

## Target outcome

Specify, test-first, the abort contract: when the finish gate fails (test
failure, infra failure, or aborted fix loop) there is no partial commit, no
residual staging in the real index, the temporary index is removed, and the
real index and working tree are byte-identical to their pre-gate state.

## Definition of done

- Boundary test at `phase_finish` (stubbed externals) asserting failure paths
  leave the real index untouched and remove the temp index.
- Real-git fixture test: run the failing gate in a temp repo, assert
  `git diff --cached --quiet` (nothing staged), no new commit on HEAD, no
  leftover `<tmp>` index file, and working-tree bytes unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Abort leaves the tree unchanged:** on gate failure there is no partial commit (`HEAD` unchanged), no residual staging (`git diff --cached --quiet` true), and the temporary index is removed.
- [ ] On gate failure the real index and working tree are byte-identical to their pre-gate state (real-git fixture assertion).
- [ ] Every exit path (success, failure, abort, exception) removes the temporary index file.
- [ ] No partial commit is created on any abort path.

# Temp-index staging in the finish gate

## Target outcome

Make the finish gate's test step validate the exact tree the commit will
produce: before the suite runs, copy the real index to a temporary file, apply
the change set to the copy (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> git add -A`), and run the
suite with `GIT_INDEX_FILE` exported so every child `git` command (including
`git ls-files` inside tests) sees the staged file set. On success the real
index receives `git add -A` and the commit proceeds — after a `git write-tree`
equality assertion proving the committed tree is the tested tree. On failure
the temp index is deleted and the real index and working tree are untouched.

## Definition of done

- `phase_finish`'s test step creates the temp index and exports `GIT_INDEX_FILE`
  into the suite subprocess environment (reaching `git ls-files` and the cache
  fingerprint), using the F3-verified scrub pass-through.
- Success path: real `git add -A`, assert `git write-tree` of the real index
  equals the fingerprint the suite ran against, then commit; temp index removed.
- Failure/abort/exception paths: temp index removed, no commit, no residual
  staging — satisfying the F5 abort contract.
- No new bypasses (`TEST_SCOPE_SKIP` etc. absent); guard ownership
  (`LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`) and the nested-run stand-down contract intact:
  delegation to `guarded_run_all` is unchanged.
- F1 (tracked-file guard) and F2 (parity) reproductions turn green-to-red as
  asserted; F3 and F5 tests pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Gate tests the would-be commit tree:** a change set that adds a file rejected by a tracked-file guard (`git ls-files` semantics) fails the finish gate, with the failing test named, instead of reporting a green full-scope pass — reproduced through the finish-gate entry point (F1 red).
- [ ] The suite runs with `GIT_INDEX_FILE` pointing at a temp index containing the change set, and the commit's tree equals the tree the suite ran against (write-tree equality asserted before commit).
- [ ] **Abort leaves the tree unchanged:** failure/abort/exception leaves no partial commit, no residual staging, and removes the temporary index (F5 green).
- [ ] No default bypass is added (`TEST_SCOPE_SKIP` etc.); guard ownership (`LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`) and the nested-run stand-down contract are retained.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`phase_finish` test step,
  `git_commit`, new temp-index helper)
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (scrub pass-through, read-only confirmation)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_commit_tree.py` (red after fix)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_abort.py` (abort contract)

## Deliverables

- Temp-index staging in the finish gate with write-tree equality and full
  cleanup.

## Dependencies

- **F1** (cross-tree reproduction), **F2** (parity reproduction),
  **F3** (env pass-through), **F5** (abort contract) — all children of
  SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2.

# Tree-fingerprint cache binding

## Target outcome

Bind the finish gate's cache key and verdict acceptance to the would-be-commit
tree, not the loose working tree. Add a `git write-tree`-based fingerprint
(operator-approved option A: tree SHA) and let the gate pass an explicit
expected fingerprint into `run_cached`/`lookup` so a cached result is accepted
only when its fingerprint matches the staged tree. Legacy/foreign entries miss
(fail closed). Other consumers (test skill CLI, audit, pre-push) are unchanged
when no fingerprint override is passed.

## Definition of done

- `skill/test_cache.py` gains `compute_tree_state(index_file)` — the SHA of
  `git write-tree` on the given index file (temp or real).
- `run_cached` / `lookup` accept an optional explicit `git_state`/fingerprint
  param; when supplied, the cache key and the lookup-match use it; a stored
  entry whose fingerprint differs, or which predates provenance metadata, is a
  miss (fresh run).
- `compute_git_state` and all existing callers keep their current behaviour
  (no override → unchanged keys).
- F4's cache-contract tests and F2's stale-entry miss scenario pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `compute_tree_state()` returns the `git write-tree` SHA for a given index file.
- [ ] **Cache determinism:** `GIT_INDEX_FILE` passes through the test skill's env scrub into child git commands (regression test), and the gate's cache key reflects the would-be-commit tree, not the loose working tree — a foreign/stale/legacy entry misses and the suite re-runs (F2/F4 green).
- [ ] Existing consumers without an override keep identical cache keys and behaviour (`tests/test_test_cache.py` and the test skill's suite unchanged).
- [ ] A green cached verdict is only ever accepted for a matching fingerprint.

## Key Files

- `skill/test_cache.py` (`compute_tree_state`, `run_cached`, `lookup`)
- `tests/test_test_cache.py` (regression home)
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (only if a passthrough param is needed for
  the delegated runner)

## Deliverables

- Tree-SHA fingerprint function + explicit-fingerprint cache binding.

## Dependencies

- **F4** (cache-contract tests), **F6** (temp-index staging, provides the
  staged index) — children of SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2.

# Verifiable verdicts in the gate report

## Target outcome

Make every finish-gate verdict self-describing: the report records (a) the tree
the suite ran against (worktree path + git fingerprint) and (b) whether the
result was served from cache, with entry metadata. A cached green is accepted
only when its fingerprint matches the would-be-commit tree; otherwise the suite
runs and the fresh verdict is recorded. Per parent AC2, no green verdict may be
accepted for a state whose suite has not run.

## Definition of done

- `phase_finish` report gains per-attempt keys: `tree` (worktree path),
  `git_fingerprint` (would-be-commit tree SHA), `cached` (bool), and when
  cached: `cache_entry` (command / completed_at / scope).
- The completion comment on the work item includes the verdict provenance.
- Cache-hit acceptance requires the fingerprint match (F7 binding); a mismatch
  forces a suite run before any green.
- F4's report-shape tests pass. Framework suites stay green: `skill/implement/
  tests/`, `skill/test/tests/`, `tests/test_test_cache.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **The gate proves its verdict:** the report records the tree it ran against (worktree path + fingerprint) and whether the result came from cache; no green verdict is accepted for a state whose suite has not run (stale/foreign cache entries must miss) — F4 report-shape tests green.
- [ ] The completion comment carries the verdict provenance (tree path, fingerprint, cached flag, cache entry metadata).
- [ ] **Existing green runs unaffected:** a clean change set passes exactly as today with a single gate suite execution (no duplicate run).
- [ ] **Testing/validation:** the framework suites pass — `skill/implement/tests/`, `skill/test/tests/`, `tests/test_test_cache.py`, plus the repository full suite at the dev-push gate.

# Baseline regression tests for full-suite resolution (test-first)

## Goal

Pin today's suite-resolution behaviour **before** the hidden skill-test rule
lands, so the "zero candidates → byte-identical" and "changed-scope
untouched" guarantees of SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB are enforced by durable green
tests — not only by inspection. This is the test-first slice of the parent:
it is written and committed green first; the behaviour changes in later
children must keep it green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Byte-identity baseline.** A parameterised test asserts
  `full_suite_commands(tmp_path)` equals the current resolved set for: a
  pytest-only repo, a pytest+node repo, an npm-only repo, and a repo with a
  pinned `suiteCommands` list; each result contains no command referencing
  `.pi/skills`.
- **AC2 — No-`.pi/skills` repo stays identical.** A test asserts a repo with
  NO `.pi/skills/*/tests` (the general case today, including the SorraAgents
  repo itself) resolves to the exact same command set once the F1 rule lands

# Detect and emit hidden skill-test pytest command

## Goal

Implement D1/D2 of SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB: discover project-local hidden skill
test directories at `<project_root>/.pi/skills/<name>/{tests,test}` and emit
exactly one additional quiet pytest command listing them, immediately after
the repo's canonical pytest command. Zero candidates → no command
(byte-identical resolution to today).

## Design constraints (from the parent's D1/D2)

- Detection probes only the two literal path levels under
  `.pi/skills/<name>/`; never scans `.claude/`, `.git/`, `.worklog/`.
- A candidate must contain at least one `*.py` (recursive, mirroring
  `repo_has_pytest_suite`).
- Candidates are collected, de-duplicated and sorted for deterministic
  command strings.
- One command (not one per directory): single cache entry, single timeout
  budget, unchanged semaphore accounting (`run_tests.py` acquires one
  host-wide slot per suite execution).
- Emission is independent of `repo_has_pytest_suite()`: a project with skill
  tests but no root `tests/` still gets the command.
- Paths are `shlex.quote`d; the command uses the canonical quiet pytest form
  (`pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings`), reusing `pytest_command()` /
  `canonicalize_quiet_test_command`.
- A code comment and docstring name the pytest default `norecursedirs`
  (`.*` → `.pi/` pruned) mechanism this compensates for.

## Acceptance Criteria (parent AC1 + AC2)

- **AC1 — Detection unit-tested.** Covers: one skill with `tests/`; one with
  `test/`; several skills (sorted, deterministic); a skill without tests; a
  `tests/` dir with no `*.py`; non-`.pi` hidden dirs ignored; a skill with
  BOTH `tests/` and `test/` (de-duplicated, deterministic).
- **AC2 — Emission unit-tested.** ≥1 candidate → exactly one additional quiet
  pytest command listing every candidate in stable order; zero candidates →
  resolution byte-identical to the pre-change baseline (AC2 of F0 stays
  green); a candidate present in a repo where `repo_has_pytest_suite()` is
  false → command still emitted; paths with spaces are quoted; the extra
  command sits immediately after the canonical pytest command and before any
  node commands.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — new `hidden_skill_test_dirs()` helper
  (near `repo_has_pytest_suite`, ~line 715) + wiring in
  `full_suite_commands()` (~line 1026)
- `skill/test/tests/test_hidden_skill_tests.py` — new: AC1/AC2 unit tests
data.title: Detect and emit hidden skill-test pytest command

# Pinned suiteCommands precedence and no-double-execution

## Goal

Implement D3 of SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB for the pinned/uncovered and
double-execution cases: a project's pinned `.pi/test-config.json`
`suiteCommands` list is returned verbatim (nothing appended) while a
machine-readable, non-fatal notice names the hidden skill test dirs the
pinned list does not cover; a candidate already collected via the project's
pytest `testpaths`/`addopts` is skipped.

## Design decisions (elaborating D3; recorded in the parent's Appendix)

- **Notice surface.** A new pure accessor `hidden_skill_test_notice(root)` (or
  `full_suite_notices(root)`) returns a machine-readable structure naming the
  uncovered directories plus a stable code (`hidden_skill_tests_uncovered`).
  `full_suite_commands()` keeps its `list[str]` signature (D4 — no consumer
  sees a signature change). `run_tests.py` surfaces the notice non-fatally:
  in `--json` output under `resolution_notices` and as a single stderr
  warning line when resolving a full suite whose `suiteCommands` is pinned.
  Exit status unchanged.
- **Skip rule (no double execution).** A candidate is "already covered" when
  a token in the project's pytest `testpaths` (INI `[pytest]` or
  `pyproject.toml` `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` form) or an `addopts` path
  token resolves to `.pi` or a strict descendant of `.pi` AND the candidate
  is a descendant-or-equal of that token (normalised, repo-relative). Tokens
  at or above the repo root (`.`, `tests`, `skill`) do NOT count as
  covering: default `norecursedirs` pruning still prevents `.pi` collection
  from those roots, so treating them as coverage would silently re-silence
  the hidden tests D1 exists to surface. Custom `norecursedirs`/`--ignore`
  overrides are out of scope (documented as such).

## Acceptance Criteria (parent AC3 + AC4)

- **AC3 — Pinned `suiteCommands` precedence proven.** A repo with
  `.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands` gets its list back verbatim (no
  append) AND `hidden_skill_test_notice()` names the uncovered hidden skill
  test dirs with a stable machine-readable code; one regression test pins
  both behaviours. An explicitly-empty pinned list is also returned verbatim
  with a notice.
- **AC4 — No double execution.** A candidate already covered by the project's
  pytest `testpaths`/`addopts` (INI and pyproject forms) is skipped: in the
  INI form the same candidate "covered" only by a token at repo root or
  above (`.`, `tests`) is still emitted; a candidate fully absent from
  config is emitted. Tests cover the INI and pyproject forms plus the
  uncovered case.
- **AC4b — Notice is non-fatal.** Resolution result and process exit status
  are unchanged whether or not a notice is present.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — notice accessor + skip-rule helper;
  `extension_suite_commands()`/`_read_test_config` readers (precedence
  inputs), `full_suite_commands()`
- `skill/test/tests/test_hidden_skill_tests.py` — AC3/AC4 tests
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` notice plumbing conventions referenced
  from `NOTICE_*` constants (non-fatal by construction)
data.title: Pinned suiteCommands precedence and no-double-execution

Implement D4/D5 of SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB: the `full` group and the default/full

Observed on 2026-10-28 (SorraAgents @ dev):
- Report claimed `Auto-fixed: 8`, listing EXE005, ISC004, PLW1510 and RUF059 findings.
- `git status` afterwards showed **no source changes at all** (only the unrelated `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` scheduled-prompt timestamp).

Verified cause: those diagnostics are *not* auto-fixable (`ruff check --fix` reports `fix: null` for EXE005/PLW1510/RUF059 and `fix.applicability: unsafe` for ISC004).

## Root cause

`skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — `_parse_ruff_fix_output` (line ~113) converts **every** diagnostic in ruff's JSON output into a `fixed_findings` entry, without inspecting `item['fix']` or `item['fix']['applicability']`. `auto_fix_files` (line ~217) then sets `fixes_applied = len(fixed_findings) > 0` and the report prints those as auto-fixes. Ruff emits all diagnostics (fixed and unfixed) in its JSON output, so the count is the number of *diagnostics seen*, not fixes applied.

`_parse_eslint_fix_output` has the same shape (counts every message; eslint's `output`/`fixed` fields are ignored).

## Expected behaviour

- Only count a finding as auto-fixed when the linter actually applied an edit: ruff `item['fix']` is not `None` **and** `fix.applicability == 'safe'` (the default for `--fix` without `--unsafe-fixes`).
- Unfixable/unsafe diagnostics should either be dropped or surfaced as *remaining* smells, so they still reach smell detection, REFACTOR comments and work items.
- `fixes_applied`, the summary's `auto_fixed` count and the human-readable report must agree with what actually changed on disk.
- Add a regression test: a file with only-unsafe / no-fix diagnostics must report `Auto-fixed: 0`, and a file with a safe fix must report `Auto-fixed: 1` and be changed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `_parse_ruff_fix_output` only records findings whose fix is present and safe.
2. A full-project run against a tree whose only diagnostics are unsafe/unfixable reports `Auto-fixed: 0`.
3. A tree with one safe fix reports `Auto-fixed: 1` and the file is modified on disk.
4. Unsafe/unfixable diagnostics are still represented in the `Remaining smells` section (or equivalent) rather than silently dropped.
5. New unit tests in `skill/refactor/tests/` cover both cases.
6. Existing `skill/refactor` tests pass.

## Notes

Discovered from the `/skill:refactor` full-scan scheduled run. The 8 flagged diagnostics are already tracked by open REFACTOR items (SA-0MVRCL0Q90016C7D, SA-0MVRBPVU1001NGDW, SA-0MVRBPY7J004GJAI, SA-0MVPTU9HG00146UV), so this item is only about report/labelling accuracy.
data.title: refactor skill reports false auto-fixes for unfixable linter diagnostics

data.description:
Counterpart of the AI_Hell discovery report **AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81**
(`discovered-from:AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81`). The defect is in agent infrastructure in this
repository — `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`. The full discovery context (observed
drive run, timeout, unrelated commits landing on `dev`) is on the AI_Hell report; this
item is the actionable fix.

## Headline

`implement.py parent` decides whether a child worktree contains work via
`_git_path_has_changes()`, which reports "has changes" whenever the worktree `HEAD`
*differs* from the parent branch. A child worktree that is merely **behind** `dev`
(HEAD != `dev`, zero commits ahead, no dirty files) is therefore classified as having
work, and `phase_parent` immediately runs `finish` on empty work — which falls back to a
full-suite run when changed-scope selection is unavailable and can fail the whole parent
run.

## Problem statement

`_git_path_has_changes(path, parent_branch, expected_dirty=())` currently returns:

1. `True` when the worktree has dirty files (outside `.worklog/` and any
   project-declared expected-dirty prefixes), else
2. the result of comparing `git rev-parse HEAD` with `git rev-parse <parent_branch>`
   (differing ⇒ `True`), and
3. `True` (fail open) when either `rev-parse` fails.

Comparison (2) conflates *ahead* with *diverged*: a clean worktree at the fork base
after three unrelated commits landed on `dev` differs from `dev` but contains no work.

Observed 2026-10-19 during the AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV epic (details on
AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81):

1. `implement.py drive` started a child and the child session was killed at the 3600 s
   timeout with a clean worktree (no edits, no commits).
2. While the drive ran, three unrelated commits landed on `dev`; the child worktree was
   three commits behind.
3. `implement.py parent` reported `Child <id> has changes — running finish subprocess...`
   and ran `finish` on empty work; the changed-scope selection was unavailable, the full
   suite (~10 min under load) failed, and the run reported `Failed to finish child`.

## Expected behaviour

A worktree with no dirty files and **no commits ahead of** the parent branch is treated
as "no work" (the child is returned as `next_child` for implementation), regardless of
how far behind it is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** `_git_path_has_changes()` returns `False` for a worktree with no uncommitted
  changes and no commits ahead of the parent branch, including when the worktree is
  behind the parent branch (covered by unit tests against real throwaway git
  repositories/worktrees).
- **AC2:** `phase_parent` does not launch a `finish` subprocess for a child whose
  worktree is behind `dev` but has no local commits; the child is reported as the next
  child to implement (unit test).
- **AC3:** Worktrees with commits ahead, or with dirty files, are still detected as
  having changes (no regression; unit tests).
- **AC4:** The documented placement-guard contract
  (`docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` §"The placement guard") is preserved: a non-terminal
  child whose worktree is clean at the parent HEAD while the main checkout holds
  uncommitted changes outside `.worklog/` still fails closed, and a worktree that holds
  the work never triggers the guard (unit tests).

## Implementation plan

1. **Tests first** — add `skill/implement/tests/test_worktree_has_changes.py`: clean at
   fork base, clean behind the parent branch, dirty file, one commit ahead, the
   `phase_parent` no-`finish` case, and the placement-guard cases (clean behind-only
   child + dirty main checkout fails closed; a worktree holding the work never triggers
   the guard). Confirm they fail against the current helper before changing it.
2. `_git_path_has_changes()` — keep the dirty-file check; replace the `HEAD != parent`
   comparison with an ahead-count test
   (`git rev-list --count <parent_branch>..HEAD` > 0). Keep failing open when the count
   cannot be computed (missing ref, git error).
3. Update the docstring (and `_has_worktree_changes()`'s docstring) to "dirty **or
   commits ahead of** the parent branch".
4. Verify the two guard call sites that consume the helper
   (`_worktree_placement_violation` in `phase_finish`, `_child_main_checkout_violation`
   in `phase_parent`/`phase_drive`) still match the documented contract (AC4); the
   step-1 tests pin the behaviour.
5. Update `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` if any wording still implies the "HEAD
   differs" rule.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_worktree_has_changes.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_extension.py`
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`

## Risks and assumptions

- The ahead-count semantics also change the placement guards' view of a behind-only
  clean worktree: with unrelated main-checkout dirt present, such a child now fails
  closed as "work done outside the worktree" instead of being silently re-run. This
  matches the documented guard contract (AC4) but should be called out in the commit
  message; if it proves disruptive for long-running drives, file a follow-up.
- Assumes the worktree's `dev` ref is available locally (it is: worktrees share the main
  checkout's refs).
data.title: implement.py: behind-only child worktree mis-detected as 'has changes' and auto-finished

Discovered during LP-0MVO35BF90021QY6 (llm worklog) via test-failure SA-0MVRNLSQT006T5GQ.

## Problem
`tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs` spawns `process.env.PYTHON || "python3"` and exercises the real `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py`, which imports `numpy` (line 117). The repo declares no Python dependency manifest (no `requirements.txt`), so on a bare interpreter the whole unit node suite fails with `transcription failed: No module named 'numpy'` — the failure was red on this host from 2026-10-15 until numpy was installed ad hoc during the item above.

## Goal
As a maintainer, I want the voice-input worker's Python dependencies declared (and/or the unit test to skip with a clear message when they are absent), so a fresh checkout's full suite is green without undocumented host setup.

## Acceptance criteria
1. The worker's Python runtime dependencies (numpy, faster-whisper) are declared in a committed manifest (e.g. `pi-client/voice-input/requirements.txt`) and referenced from the voice-input README setup table.
2. `tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs` either documents the install step in its header or skips (with an explicit, non-silent message) when the resolved interpreter cannot import the required modules.
3. Full suite is green on an interpreter provisioned only from the committed manifest (verified via the test skill; no ad-hoc pip installs).

## Out of scope
Changing the worker's transcription behaviour or its stub-based test contract.

## Related
- SA-0MVRNLSQT006T5GQ — the test-failure item that surfaced this.
- LP-0MVO35BF90021QY6 — llm worklog item whose dev-push gate was blocked by it (code in SorraAgents).
