# implement.py parent/drive starts children of a parent whose own outbound depends-on edge is unmet

discovered-from:RISE-0MVPY83CA00335W3 (TCE repo, cross-project reference only — the
edge below is recorded in the TCE worklog; the bug lives in this repo's
`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`).

## Problem statement

`phase_parent()` / `phase_drive()` build their dependency graph **only from the
children's own outbound (`depends-on`) edges** (`wl_dep_blockers(cid)` per child
at `implement.py:5688`). The parent item's **own** outbound edges are never
consulted, and the parent's `status: blocked` is never checked. So a parent that
is deliberately `blocked` on an unmet dependency (a producer-mandated sequencing
hold) will still have its first startable child **started**, a worktree created,
and code implemented — silently overriding the producer's decision and editing
files the still-pending dependency is working on.

Real-world repro: TCE epic **RISE-0MVPY83CA00335W3** (*Remove the obsolete
'latestDeath' progression mechanic*) has `status: blocked` with outbound edge
→ **RISE-0MVN2V6YO002AHL4** (`in-progress`, itself an epic with 4 non-terminal
children editing the same files), per producer decision "land after
RISE-0MVN2V6YO002AHL4" (P-Q3=B, 2026-10-28). `/skill:implement
RISE-0MVPY83CA00335W3` was dispatched while the item was `blocked`; evaluation
showed `phase_parent` would classify F1 (`RISE-0MVRZKAKN002SFWM`, open) as
startable and create its worktree, ignoring the unmet edge. Verification code
path: `wl_dep_blockers` has a single call site (child classification); neither
`phase_start`, `phase_parent` nor `phase_drive` consults the parent's own
outbound edges or its status.

Note the distinction from SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T's documented assumption:
"cross-project external blockers are coordination notes" — that covers edges
recorded **on children** to other repos. This gap is a **same-project edge on
the parent itself**, which currently is not even reported, and a parent-level
`blocked` status that gates nothing.

## Users

- **Producer** — "As a producer, I want my explicit sequencing decisions
  (`depends-on` edges, `blocked` status, P-Q3-style holds) respected by the
  implement orchestrator, so a `blocked` epic never starts editing the same
  files an in-progress dependency still owns."
- **Agent/operator** — "As an agent, I want the orchestrator to tell me why a
  parent cannot start children (blocked by <id>), instead of creating a
  conflicting worktree mid-flight."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `phase_parent` (and therefore `phase_drive`) resolves the parent's own outbound edges via `wl_dep_blockers(<parent>)` **before** classifying any child. If any outbound blocker is non-terminal, no child worktree is created; the report carries a `parent_blocked_by` list (ids + statuses), and the per-child classifications are skipped/reported as blocked. `phase_start` on a leaf whose own outbound edges are unmet behaves likewise.
2. A parent with `status: blocked` and an unmet outbound edge produces a `blocked` verdict (not `ok` + `next_child`) dedicated to that reason; the automation-friendly JSON includes the blocker ids.
3. Behaviour is unchanged when the parent has no outbound edges or all outbound blockers are terminal (`_is_terminal_child` semantics) — no regression to the existing in-chain ordering (SA-0MVO6UL70000HT0J) or parent-advance rules.
4. Regression tests cover: (a) parent blocked by one non-terminal outbound blocker → no child started, report names the blocker; (b) parent with terminal/absent outbound blockers → prior behaviour; (c) leaf item whose own blockers are unmet → start refuses with the blocker list.
5. `SKILL.md` Step 6.1 documents that a parent whose own outbound blockers are unmet waits (mirrors the portrait of `wl next` / `blocked` status), and the external-blocker "coordination note" wording is clarified to include same-project parent-level edges.

## Minimal implementation

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`:
  - `phase_parent` (~line 5569): after fetching the parent (Step 3), call
    `parent_blockers = wl_dep_blockers(work_item_id)`; **before** Step 5
    (child classification), if any outbound blocker is non-terminal
    (`_is_terminal_status` / hard-deleted semantics from `_is_terminal_child`),
    emit the `blocked`-verdict report (`parent_blocked_by` = ids + statuses; no
    `next_child`, no worktree creation) and return early. Terminal or
    soft-deleted blockers are ignored.
  - `phase_drive` (~line 6637): when a parent report carries
    `parent_blocked_by`, copy it into the drive report and stop **without**
    spawning a session (distinct from a hard `failed_child` failure).
  - `phase_start` (~line 4254): same outbound-blocker gate for leaf items,
    placed **before** the Step 3 claim (so an unmet leaf blocker never leaves
    the item claimed `in_progress` with no worktree); refuse with the blocker
    list.
- `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py` (or a new
  `tests/test_implement_parent_outbound_gate.py`): regression cases per AC4,
  using the injectable runner pattern already used for the phase_parent tests
  (`fake_wl_dep_blockers` keyed by item id — extend to answer for the parent
  id too).
- `skill/implement/tests/`: regression case for the `phase_start` leaf gate
  (same target file family as `test_phase_start_claim.py`).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`: Step 6.1 wording per AC5.
- **Ordering (test-first):** write the AC4 regression tests first, then the
  implementation gates (TDD, per the implement skill).

## Key files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `wl_dep_blockers` (~line 506; its
  only current call site is the child classification at line 5688),
  `phase_start` (~line 4254, claim at Step 3), `phase_parent` (~line 5569,
  child classification at Step 5), `phase_drive` (~line 6637, parent-report
  consumption)
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Step 6.1
- `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py` — phase_parent regression tests
  (injectable `wl_dep_blockers` runner); `skill/implement/tests/` for the
  `phase_start` gate case

## Assumptions (planning session, 2026-10-28)

- A1 — A parent with `status: blocked` and **no** outbound edges also gates
  starting (consistent with `wl next` skipping blocked items). The ACs phrase
  the requirement as blocked + unmet edge; honouring a plain `blocked` status
  is the safe default and is flagged for producer confirmation in the plan
  report.
- A2 — Machine-readable "blocked verdict": the parent report signals the
  blocked outcome via `parent_blocked_by` present, no `next_child`, no
  `parent_advanced`, with `success` kept true (soft stop mirroring the existing
  sibling-blocked path); `phase_drive` forwards `parent_blocked_by` so callers
  can distinguish `blocked` (soft) from `failed` (hard).
- A3 — The `phase_start` leaf gate sits before its claim step so a blocked leaf
  never ends up `in_progress` with no worktree.

## Related work

- SA-0MVO6UL70000HT0J (open) — sibling gap in the same function (terminal
  blockers still gate topological readiness); complementary, not overlapping:
  that item fixes ordering over non-terminal in-chain blockers, this item gates
  starting on parent-level outbound blockers.
- SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T (completed) — introduced parent recursion with the
  "external blockers are coordination notes" assumption; that assumption needs
  the clarification in AC5.

## Notes

- The TCE item is **not** fixed by this item; it stays `blocked` until
  RISE-0MVN2V6YO002AHL4 lands, which is the correct end state — this item only
  makes the orchestrator honour that state.

## Plan: changelog (plan skill, 2026-10-28)

- AC bullets unwrapped to single lines (tooling parses each AC as one line).
- Key Files corrected: `skill/implement/tests/` → `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py` (real phase_parent regression suite) + `skill/implement/tests/` for the start-gate case; line refs updated (phase_start ~4254, phase_parent ~5569, phase_drive ~6637, wl_dep_blockers ~506).
- Minimal implementation extended with gate placement (before Step 5 classification; before `phase_start` Step 3 claim), `phase_drive` `parent_blocked_by` forwarding, and test-first ordering.
- Assumptions A1–A3 recorded. No new child items created (S-sized, single-file change; coverage review: proceed, 100% covered).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers (planning, 2026-10-28)

- No operator interview occurred (downtime dispatch). No clarifying questions were required to reach `plan_complete`.
- OPEN ITEM (directed to producer, non-blocking): confirm Assumption A1 — should a parent whose `status: blocked` has **no** outbound edges also refuse to start children? Recorded answer (plan, recommended default): yes, matched to `wl next` blocked-item semantics; the implementation options are scoped in A1/A2.

## Goal

Five tests in `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` are source-code-grep / structural anti-patterns (per `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`). Rework them to assert observable behaviour, or delete them if the behaviour is already covered elsewhere. Discovered by the test-churn pruning review (analyser v2.1.0, dev @ 7875214).

## Affected tests (line numbers at discovery)

- L427 `check-audit-gate: SKILL.md documents the audit gating step` — reads SKILL.md text, asserts word substrings.
- L462 `check-audit-gate: run-release.js imports checkAuditReadyToClose` — reads source text, asserts string presence (the import behaviour is already exercised by the module-import behaviour tests).
- L478 `check-audit-gate: run-release.js uses exit code 6 for audit gate failure` — reads source text, asserts `'return 6'`/similar. Behaviour should be verified by exercising run-release against a failing audit gate.
- L496 `check-audit-gate: SKILL.md documents exit code 6 for audit gate` — includes a near-placeholder catch-all condition `(content.includes('6') && content.includes('audit'))` that matches almost any content.
- L865 `check-audit-gate: checkProducerReviewStatus has JSDoc comment` — structural-only test asserting documentation presence, not observable behaviour.

The file is otherwise healthy (89 tests, 255 asserts, real behaviour via `await import(MODULE_PATH)` + `execFileSync`); the fix must not remove the file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The five tests above either pin observable behaviour (running the real module/gate and asserting output/exit codes) or are deleted.
- [ ] No test in the file reads a source or markdown file and asserts a substring of its text.
- [ ] The near-placeholder catch-all condition (L496) is eliminated.
- [ ] Behaviour previously pinned by each reworked test remains covered by a live test somewhere in the suite.
- [ ] Full suite passes after the change (run via the test skill).

data.description:
## Goal

Users of the refactor skill need to know whether the project's **tests are
worth keeping**, not only whether the source has code smells. Integrate the
`test-churn` skill into the refactor workflow so every refactor run also
produces test-churn metrics (rewrite ratio, test growth, per-area churn), and
surface that evidence in the refactor skill's final report.

## Problem Statement

The refactor skill currently analyses **source code only** (`refactor.py` scans
`.py`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`; tests are scanned for
smells like any other code, but their *value* is never assessed). Test-value
evidence exists but only on demand, via the separate `test-churn` skill
(`skill`-external, script `test_churn_analysis.py`). Nothing in the refactor
workflow detects a suite that is growing without manifest benefit, so the
`refactor` run cannot report the pruning signal documented in the test-churn
skill's pruning review workflow.

## User Stories

- **Agent running a refactor:** "When I run the refactor skill, the report tells
  me whether the test suite is growing without benefit, so I can file a
  pruning work item without remembering to run a second skill."
- **Operator / producer:** "Every refactor report carries reproducible test
  churn numbers, so TDD-ROI evidence is produced continuously rather than
  requested ad hoc."
- **Maintainer:** "The integration is additive — a missing/broken test-churn
  script never fails a refactor run, and `--no-churn` restores today's exact
  behaviour."

## Proposed Behaviour

1. `refactor.py` invokes the test-churn analyser as an **additional pipeline
   stage** after smell detection, for both invocation modes (full scan and
   session boundary).
2. A new `--no-churn` flag skips the stage (mirroring `--no-sync`,
   `--no-linter`, `--no-llm`) for offline/deterministic/fast runs.
3. The **human report** gains a test-churn section showing at minimum: modified
   only rewrite ratio, including-new rewrite ratio, net test lines/files
   growth, and the flagged top-churn areas.
4. The **`--json` report** gains a `test_churn` key carrying the analyser's
   `test_churn_data.json` payload (or a documented failure/omitted marker).
5. The stage is **non-fatal**: an unavailable analyser, non-git directory, or
   analyser error logs a warning and the refactor run continues with unchanged
   exit-code semantics (mirroring the existing `wl sync` policy).
6. `SKILL.md` documents the stage, the flag, the report section and the
   non-fatal policy, and cross-references the test-churn skill.

## Constraint: skill boundary

`skill/refactor/` must not import `test_churn_analysis.py` from the installed
skill directory. The integration must resolve the analyser at runtime (the
documented `$(skill_path test-churn)` pattern) or invoke it as a subprocess, so
this repo stays the canonical source and no copy of the analyser is vendored.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A full-project `/skill:refactor` run renders a test-churn section in the human report containing the modified-only rewrite ratio, the including-new rewrite ratio, and net test line growth.
- [ ] AC2: `refactor.py --json` emits a `test_churn` key whose value contains the analyser metrics (at minimum the two rewrite ratios and `growth_metrics`).
- [ ] AC3: `--no-churn` skips the stage and produces a report byte-identical to current behaviour (no test-churn section, no `test_churn` key).
- [ ] AC4: When the analyser is unavailable or returns non-zero, the run logs a warning, completes successfully, and reports the stage as unavailable — the refactor exit code is unchanged.
- [ ] AC5: `session boundary` mode (`refactor.py <work-item-id>`) also runs the stage, and its work-item `StatusLifecycle` behaviour is unchanged (item never left `in_progress`).
- [ ] AC6: New tests cover the added stage (report rendering, JSON key, `--no-churn`, and the non-fatal failure path) without shelling out to the real analyser — following the test-writing guidelines (no source-grep or self-referential tests).
- [ ] AC7: `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` documents the stage, flag, report section, non-fatal policy and the cross-reference to the test-churn skill.
- [ ] AC8: No code under `skill/refactor/` imports from an installed skill path; the analyser is resolved at runtime or invoked as a subprocess.
- [ ] AC9: Full suite passes (run via the test skill).
data.title: Integrate test-churn analysis into the refactor skill and report

data.description:
## Goal

Make the project's test suite **earn its runtime**: every remaining test should
pin observable behaviour, and no test should exist that cannot fail for a
reason a developer cares about. This epic covers a complete, evidence-led
test-value refactor of the suite — measure, classify, prune, rework, and guard
against reintroduction — rather than the current one-file-at-a-time ad-hoc
cleanups.

## Problem Statement

The suite has grown substantially and carries demonstrable waste:

- **Measured growth (test-churn analyser v2.1.0, `dev` @ 7875214):**
  208,809 test lines added vs 71,787 deleted → **net +137,022 lines**;
  498 test files added vs 114 deleted → **net +384 files**. Net growth is
  positive in **every** calendar quarter, accelerating in 2026-Q3 (+55,892)
  and 2026-Q4 (+38,024).
- **Rewrite ratio is LOW** (14.0% modified-only, 6.2% including new files),
  which means tests largely *survive* feature evolution. That is good news for
  TDD value, but it means growth is dominated by **additive accumulation**,
  not churn — precisely the pattern where dead, duplicated and
  source-grep/structural tests survive unnoticed because nothing forces them
  to be re-examined.
- **Known confirmed offenders found so far:** 5 source-grep / structural
  anti-pattern tests in `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`
  (SA-0MVSCS0M80007X23); 15 test helpers invoking real `git` non-hermetically
  (already tracked, SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0).
- There is **no standing mechanism** that classifies test files by value, so
  every finding so far depended on a human/agent choosing to look.

## Why an epic (not another leaf)

Value assessment is a repeatable pipeline — detect candidates, prove they no
longer map to behaviour, prune or rework, verify nothing broke, and prevent
reintroduction. That needs coordinated child items across measurement,
classification, remediation, and guarding; single-file items cannot deliver it.

## Existing related work — do NOT duplicate

These items already exist and must be **depended on / coordinated with**, not
recreated:

- `SA-0MVSCS0M80007X23` — rework the 5 source-grep tests in `test-check-audit-gate.mjs`.
- `SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0` — migrate 15 raw-git test helpers to `git_sandbox` (hermeticity, not value).
- `SA-0MVSCZ2U500420IC` — integrate test-churn metrics into the refactor skill.
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing on top-churn modules (evidence arm).
- `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G` — prefer interface/behaviour assertions over `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on internal collaborators.
- `SA-0MV28WYLU001BMFU` — scheduled test-churn runs across projects.

## Scope

1. **Measure (baseline).** Capture the test-churn baseline (rewrite ratios, net
   growth, per-area churn, suite wall-clock runtime, per-file runtime) so every
   later change is provable.
2. **Classify.** Run the code-path evaluator (`skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`)
   plus the `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` anti-pattern checklist
   over the whole suite, recording a **keep / rework / prune** verdict per file.
3. **Prove.** For each prune candidate, demonstrate the behaviour it pins is
   either not observable, already covered elsewhere, or no longer exists
   (`git blame` + coverage grep of the public API). Mutation testing is the
   tie-breaker where provenance is unclear.
4. **Remediate.** Prune dead/duplicate tests; rework devalued ones (source-grep
   → behaviour; placeholder → real assertion or delete; simulation → exercise
   production code).
5. **Guard.** Add a regression guard so the pruned anti-pattern classes cannot
   be reintroduced silently, and so future additions are screened.
6. **Report.** Record before/after metrics so the value delivered is auditable.

## Non-goals

- Not a coverage-maximisation exercise: reducing test count is acceptable and
  expected where tests pin nothing.
- Not a rewrite of the audit/refactor/implement skills' behaviour.
- Not the hermeticity migration (tracked separately in `SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A baseline is recorded in this item: modified-only and including-new rewrite ratios, net test file/line growth, suite wall-clock runtime, and the evaluator/checklist verdict for every test file in scope.
- [ ] AC2: Every test file in scope carries an explicit keep / rework / prune verdict with its justifying evidence, and the totals reconcile (verdicts sum to files in scope).
- [ ] AC3: Every prune candidate has written evidence that the behaviour it pinned is not observable, already covered via the public API, or gone — no test is deleted on suspicion alone.
- [ ] AC4: All `prune`-verdict tests are removed and all `rework`-verdict tests are converted to observable-behaviour assertions; no remaining test file reads a source/markdown file and asserts on its text.
- [ ] AC5: After the refactor, `evaluate_usefulness.py` reports no `remove` verdict for any scanned test file, and the suite contains zero placeholder or zero-assertion tests.
- [ ] AC6: The suite is green (full scope, run via the test skill) and no acceptance criterion of any work item loses coverage — demonstrated by the audits and a before/after coverage map, not by assertion counts.
- [ ] AC7: Suite wall-clock runtime is measurably reduced (or, where runtime rises, the item documents why the surviving tests justify it) with before/after numbers.
- [ ] AC8: A regression guard fails the suite if a newly added test matches a pruned anti-pattern class (source-grep, placeholder, zero-assertion, self-referential simulation), without becoming a source-grep test itself.
- [ ] AC9: The pruning workflow in `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` and the anti-patterns in `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` are updated with anything this pass learned (new anti-patterns, refined criteria).
- [ ] AC10: Full project test suite passes with the changes, and the final report records the before/after deltas.

## Risks

- **Removing a useful test is a regression; keeping a dead one only costs
  runtime.** Pruning criteria stay conservative — when in doubt, keep the test
  and file a work item.
- Deleting tests can raise apparent coverage drops: coverage is judged by
  behaviour/AC mapping (AC6), never by percentage alone.
- Suite-wide classification is expensive; it must be batched with bounded
  fan-out per the test execution policy (never ad-hoc full suites).

## Notes

Discovered during a test-churn pruning review, 2026-10-28. Priority is medium
because the measured rewrite ratio is already LOW (tests largely survive
feature evolution) — the waste here is accumulation, not thrash, so this is
valuable hygiene rather than an emergency. Children to be created at plan
stage.

# Goal

Make the in-main-slot child-screen resume cycle actually work end to end: after the invoking session performs the emitted `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` child screens and persists each child audit, a re-run of the parent audit must **collect** those child verdicts (zero pi calls), clear the `Child screens pending: N (main-slot)` gate and remove `<id>.pending-screens.json`. Today that resume cycle is unreachable, so the pending gate is permanent for the item.

# Problem statement

Observed during a real production audit (LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0 in the `llm` project, 2026-10-28 23:46 → 2026-10-29 00:01 UTC, runner log `~/.audit_debug/llm/LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0-20261028-234657.log`):

1. The run finished in in-main-slot mode with `Ready to close: No`, the header line `Child screens pending: 2 (main-slot) — LP-0MVOG7IP80003MLV, LP-0MVOG7IX6006MZ23`, and the signal `.worklog/audit-checkpoints/LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0.pending-screens.json`.
2. The invoking session performed both child screens and persisted both child audits **with v2 content fingerprints** (`wl audit-show` verified: one `Ready to close: No`, one `Ready to close: Yes`).
3. The documented re-run (`audit_runner.py issue LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0`) then short-circuited:

   ```
   Skipping: audit still fresh — Ready to close: No (audited 2026-10-29T00:01:32.443Z)
   ```

   because `_check_audit_freshness()` compares the item's v2 content fingerprint and the parent's title/description are unchanged — a report whose own header says "Child screens pending" counts as a *final, fresh* verdict. The pipeline never resumes, the two persisted child audits are never consulted, and the signal file stays on disk (a later herdr dispatch will read the same fresh report and exit the same way).

The result contradicts the documented contract ("re-running the parent audit then reuses the fresh child audit with zero pi calls" — `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, "Child audits in the main LLM slot"), and it leaves the item permanently clamped by a gate that can no longer clear.

# Root cause

Two independent defects in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`:

**D1 — the item-level freshness gate ignores the pending-screens signal.** `cmd_issue()` (`:10283-10300`) calls `_check_audit_freshness()` (`:2054`) before anything else and returns the stored report when the content fingerprint matches. The pending-screens signal is only *read* much later, during report assembly (`_read_pending_screens_signal`, `:5900`), and only to classify unserviced children — it can never influence the gate. So the one state that must not be treated as a final verdict (screens outstanding) is exactly the state that is treated as fresh.

**D2 — a `phase1_children` checkpoint resume replays the placeholder ACs.** `_run_phase_children()` (`:12034-12044`) sets `phase1_checkpointed` from `checkpoint.phase_status(PHASE_CHILDREN) == STATUS_COMPLETED`; the resume path (`:12076-12095`) then restores `child_results` from `checkpoint.accumulated_state()`, whose per-child `ac_results` still carry `VERDICT_PARTIAL` + `MAIN_SLOT_PENDING_EVIDENCE`. `_pending_main_slot_child_ids()` (`:5749`) therefore re-derives the same pending list, so even after D1 is fixed the gate re-fires and the persisted child audits are never reached. The reuse path that would pick them up already exists (`_get_child_audit_verdict()` at `:12159` → `_child_acs_from_own_audit()`), it is simply never executed on resume.

# Desired change

1. **D1:** in `cmd_issue()`, when a pending-screens signal exists for the item (`_read_pending_screens_signal(issue_id, owning_root, ctx.checkpoint_dir)` is non-empty), do **not** take the freshness short-circuit — fall through to the pipeline so the checkpoint resume runs. A report whose `pending_child_screens` are outstanding is not a final verdict. Keep `--force` behaviour unchanged, and make sure the `--do-not-persist` freshness-refresh path cannot re-publish "fresh" for such a run.
2. **D2:** when the restored `child_results` of a `phase1_children` checkpoint contain `MAIN_SLOT_PENDING_EVIDENCE`, treat that phase as **not** complete for this run (or equivalently re-resolve those children before the pending gate is computed), so the existing child-verdict reuse path runs: each pending child's freshly persisted audit is reused (`reused_from` / `child_audit_ready`/`child_audit_not_ready` set, `ac_results` from `_child_acs_from_own_audit()`), zero pi calls are made, `_pending_main_slot_child_ids()` returns empty and `_write_pending_screens_signal([])` (`:13011`) removes the signal.
3. Children with **no** fresh stored audit must remain pending (unchanged conservative behaviour); the parent's readiness must still be `No` while any screen is genuinely outstanding.
4. Do not weaken: the child-audit execution gate (`Ready to close: Yes` impossible while screens are pending), the unserviced-in-main-slot classification (SA-0MVAWFUU0004VW45: `unserviced_in_main_slot` / `not_assessed` reason codes), the no-side-effect restore rule, or `--force` semantics (force still bypasses child reuse).

# Acceptance criteria

- AC1: With a stored parent audit that is fresh by content fingerprint **and** a `<id>.pending-screens.json` listing ≥ 1 child, `audit_runner.py issue <id>` does not print `Skipping: audit still fresh` and proceeds to the pipeline (unit test with a mocked `wl`, asserting `_check_audit_freshness` is not taken as the terminal path).
- AC2: After the pending child screens have been serviced (fresh child audits persisted with v2 fingerprints) and the parent re-run on the same HEAD, the resulting report contains **no** `Child screens pending:` gate, `pending_child_screens` is empty in the JSON payload, and `<id>.pending-screens.json` is removed from the checkpoint directory. No child-screening pi call is made for a child with a fresh stored audit.
- AC3: A child whose screens were serviced but whose stored audit verdict is `Ready to close: No` is reported as assessed / `child_audit_not_ready` (not `not_assessed`), and still blocks the parent's readiness.
- AC4: A child with no stored audit, or with a stale stored audit (changed title/description or `--force`), still appears as pending — the new fast path never fabricates a serviced state.
- AC5: Regression coverage: `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` (signal-aware gate), `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` (checkpoint-resume reuse + signal removal, `wl` mocked — no real pi child subprocess), `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_reason_diagnostics.py` (assessed vs `not_assessed`). The full suite passes via the test skill.
- AC6: `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (and the audit reference doc if present) documents the now-working resume cycle — including the case where the invoking session services the screens in the *same* session as the first run, and the case where a later session services them — so the "perform the screen, persist the child audit, re-run the parent" instruction is truthful.

# Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `cmd_issue()` freshness gate (`:10283`), `_check_audit_freshness()` (`:2054`), `_read_pending_screens_signal()` (`:5900`), `_write_pending_screens_signal()` (`:5773`, call site `:13011`), `_pending_main_slot_child_ids()` (`:5749`), `_run_phase_children()` checkpoint restore (`:12034-12095`), child-verdict reuse (`:12159`).
- `skill/audit/scripts/checkpoint_store.py` — `PHASE_CHILDREN` / `STATUS_COMPLETED` semantics (`:55-58`), `accumulated_state()`, `phase_status()`.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py`, `test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py`, `test_audit_runner_child_reason_diagnostics.py` — new/updated regression tests.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — the in-main-slot contract paragraph to reconcile with the fixed behaviour.

# Constraints

- Behaviour-preserving for the separate-process child mode (`--no-child-in-main-slot`) and for `--force`.
- Never spawn a real child `pi` subprocess in the new tests (mock `subprocess.run` / the child-audit entry point, per `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`).
- No change to verdict vocabulary, the readiness criteria, or persistence ordering (comments before `wl audit-set`).

# Definition of Done / Verification

- Reproduction first: a failing test that drives `_run_phase_children` with a `phase1_children`-completed checkpoint whose children carry `MAIN_SLOT_PENDING_EVIDENCE`, plus a fresh child audit stubbed in `wl audit-show`, and asserts the pending list is empty afterwards (today it is not).
- AC1–AC5 green; full suite green via the test skill; SKILL.md updated (AC6).

# Evidence

- Production case: `llm` work item LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0 — runner log `~/.audit_debug/llm/LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0-20261028-234657.log`, persisted parent report header `Child screens pending: 2 (main-slot) — LP-0MVOG7IP80003MLV, LP-0MVOG7IX6006MZ23`, served children LP-0MVOG7IP80003MLV (`No`) and LP-0MVOG7IX6006MZ23 (`Yes`), leftover signal `.worklog/audit-checkpoints/LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0.pending-screens.json`.
- Prior related work (all completed, none covers resume-after-service): SA-0MU32TE120012T49 (child-audit execution gate + signal), SA-0MVAWFUU0004VW45 / SA-0MVAWFYZE0040SQ3 (unserviced-child classification), SA-0MUH6H87Z001HYJ7 (stale-child re-audit), SA-0MT6EZUS9004FJ9T (phase checkpoints).

# implement.py finish deletes a plain leaf session's cwd, breaking its post-finish steps

`discovered-from:SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR` — split out of the driven-session worktree-removal fix at producer request (Q2 of that item's intake). Same root cause, different caller: here the *session that invoked finish* is the operator's own agent session, not a driver-spawned child.

**Headline:** `implement.py finish` must not leave a plain leaf session unable to run any command: after finish removes the worktree, Pi's bash tool refuses every call in that session, so the report, the worklog comment and the post-push verification steps all fail.

## Problem statement

`phase_finish` removes the worktree after the dev push (Step 7, `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:5322`). In the plain leaf flow the finishing process is a **child** of the agent session (`bash` tool), and that session's cwd *is* the worktree. `_remove_worktree` chdirs only the finish process out of the tree (`:2364-2376`), so the session keeps a deleted cwd: Pi's bash tool then rejects every command with `Working directory does not exist: … / Cannot execute bash commands.` while absolute-path `read`/`write` still work. The session is reduced to a degraded loop exactly when it should be writing its completion comment, rendering its report and verifying the pushed commit.

## Users and user stories

- **Implement agent (plain leaf item)** — "As an agent finishing a leaf work item, I want my post-finish steps to run normally, so I do not have to invent absolute-path workarounds for the report and the post-push verification."
- **Operator / reviewer** — "As the reviewer, I want the session's final report and verification evidence produced by the workflow rather than improvised, so I can trust what I read."
- **Maintainer** — "As the maintainer, I want one deterministic rule for when a worktree may be deleted relative to the session that owns it."

## Recorded evidence

- **RISE-0MVPZ31UJ000BC33** (session `01a1840b-13a6-71a0-9153-f89e8dd2dfee`, TCE repo): the session hit `Working directory does not exist` **8 times** after its foreground `implement.py finish`, then worked around it — its own transcript notes "After that bash won't work, so do it last", and it removed a placeholder directory as its final action.
- Same failure mode documented in `SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR` for driven sessions (where it also wedges the drive loop); that item fixes the driven case only.

## Desired change (direction, not a fixed design)

The driven case is solved by deferring removal to the driver. The plain case has no external owner, so the options are:

1. **Defer to the session's own last step** — finish keeps the worktree and the implement skill's finish step ends with an explicit, runnable cleanup instruction (`git worktree remove … && git worktree prune`) that the *session* performs as its final action, after the comment, report and verification are done.
2. **Defer to a separate cleanup pass** — finish always defers; the cleanup skill / `implement.py` gains a `cleanup` action that removes worktrees of terminal items, run by the operator or the next workflow step.
3. **Make finish's removal non-fatal to the session** — keep removing, but ensure nothing after it needs bash (move report rendering/comment/verification *before* removal inside finish). Cheapest, but leaves the session's cwd dead for any later operator-driven interaction.

A design decision is required at intake/plan time; option 1 or 2 is expected to fit the existing `--keep-worktree` hatch added by SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — No dead cwd after finish in the plain flow.** A plain leaf session can still run bash commands after `implement.py finish` returns (or the workflow guarantees nothing after finish needs bash — depending on the chosen option), verified by a test that drives `phase_finish` and asserts the session-visible worktree state.
- [ ] **AC2 — Cleanup still happens deterministically.** Whichever option is chosen, a finished leaf item's worktree is removed by a named step within the same workflow run (session final action or cleanup pass), with the removal recorded in the finish/cleanup report.
- [ ] **AC3 — Consistency with the driven fix.** The mechanism reuses the deferral predicate/flag introduced by SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR (`IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE`, `--keep-worktree` / `IMPLEMENT_KEEP_WORKTREE`) rather than adding a third removal path.
- [ ] **AC4 — Interruption safety.** An interrupted workflow leaves the worktree present and reported (never half-removed), and a repeat run is idempotent.
- [ ] **AC5 — Documentation.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (finish step cleanup instructions), `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` and `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` state the ownership rule for the plain flow.
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing/validation criterion.** New tests plus the changed-scope suite pass via the test skill (`/skill:test`), and the dev-push full-suite gate is green for the pushed commit.
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Do **not** change the driven-session behaviour delivered by SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR; this item is the non-driven path only.
- Reuse `_remove_worktree`, `cleanup_worktree_processes` and the existing safety gates; no new deletion mechanism, no `rm -rf`-style shortcuts.
- Never remove a worktree that is dirty or whose item is non-terminal.
- Pi core's bash-tool behaviour on a missing cwd is out of scope (a Pi-core limitation, not fixable here).
- **Out of scope:** the pane transport, `hygiene_check.sh` rework, branch deletion.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` Step 6b/7 and the finish-step ordering, plus the deferral predicate shared with SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — finish-step cleanup instructions (currently a manual `git worktree remove` block, `SKILL.md:811`).
- `skill/implement/tests/` — extend the finish test harness (`test_finish_no_diff_status.py` style) for the plain-flow behaviour.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — ownership rule for the plain flow.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR** — "implement.py finish removes the worktree under a driven child session, wedging it" (open, parent of this split): fixes the driven path; this item must reuse its deferral mechanism.
- **SA-0MVJC5KNT0044L2B** — finish SIGTERMing itself in `wl cleanup-worktree` (completed): the self-exclusion contract around Step 6b.
- **SA-0MRTSO5W8005ZGA7** — added the worktree process cleanup call to the workflow (completed).
- **RISE-0MVPZ31UJ000BC33** — the plain-flow session that hit the deleted cwd 8 times (completed).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Options 1/2 leave worktrees behind on interruption** — mitigated by AC4 and by the cleanup skill.
- **Doc/instruction drift:** `SKILL.md` currently instructs the agent to run `git worktree remove` itself after pushing, duplicating finish's removal; the chosen option must make the instruction and the code agree.
- **Assumption:** the operator's session is the only other holder of the worktree cwd in the plain flow (no other process needs it), so removal timing is purely about the session's own remaining steps.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "just make Pi tolerate a deleted cwd" is a Pi-core change — record it, do not attempt it here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Scope split.** *Answer (producer, during SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR intake): "driver only, raise a follow up item for the plain leaf flow".* This item is that follow-up; the driven path is SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR.
- **Q2 (OPEN QUESTION, for planning) — Which cleanup owner for the plain flow?** (1) the session's own final step, (2) a separate cleanup pass, (3) move everything that needs bash before removal inside finish. Recommended: **(1)**, because it keeps a single workflow run responsible for its own cleanup and reuses the `--keep-worktree` hatch; (2) becomes preferable if the cleanup skill is the operator's normal sweep.
- **Q3 (answered by research) — Is the failure a hang?** No: bash is refused for the rest of the session while absolute-path file tools still work; the session degrades but does not block (RISE-0MVPZ31UJ000BC33's workaround).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR** – implement.py finish removes the worktree under a driven child session, wedging it (in-progress)
- **SA-0MVJC5KNT0044L2B** – implement.py finish SIGTERMs itself in wl cleanup-worktree, stranding the dev push (completed)
- **SA-0MVMMHG9Z004F2ED** – implement.py finish refuses to remove a resumed worktree because phase_start stores the worktree as repo_root (open)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: absolute, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+267 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: absolute, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+253 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0mvjc5knt0044l2b, absolute, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+246 more)

# Finish gate: classify timeouts and kills distinctly from code failures, and report test-slot queue wait separately

Discovered-from: **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6** (tce-main-street) — this item owns that work item's **AC3**.

## Problem

On the shared multi-agent host a suite run can (a) exceed `timeoutPerCommand`, or (b) be killed (OOM / worker crash) without producing parsable failures. Both are currently presented as code failures, and the host-wide test semaphore's queue wait is indistinguishable from test time.

Measured evidence on tce-main-street (`MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6`):

- `/tmp/ms0mvpy2-finish.log` — `implement.py finish` reported `Test run 1/3 failed (unknown)`, `failures: []`, `notices: []` after `phase_finish` 2215 s. A non-zero/killed run with no parsable failures becomes `GATE_FAILURE_UNKNOWN`.
- `/tmp/ms0mvpy2ydq-finish.log` — `reason: slot_contention` after a 2400 s slot wait.
- `/tmp/ms0mvpy2-warm3.log` — `slot_busy` after a 1500 s wait.
- `/tmp/ms0mvpy2-full.log` — a green full suite measured `elapsed: 2846.6 s`.

Consequence: an agent cannot tell whether to fix code, raise the timeout, or wait for a slot, so it retries blindly. The `timeoutPerCommand` remediation documented in `.pi/test-config.json`-based repos ("set it high enough to cover the full suite with headroom") is meaningless while a kill and a clean `TimeoutExpired` are reported identically.

## Requirements (carried from MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6 AC3)

1. A suite that exceeds `timeoutPerCommand`, or is killed without parsable failures, is reported as an **infrastructure/timeout** condition — never `reason: unknown` with `failures: []`.
2. The report includes the **configured timeout** and the **elapsed time**.
3. The **semaphore queue wait** is reported separately as its own duration (e.g. `slot_busy` seconds), not folded into suite elapsed time.
4. Queue wait is **not charged to the suite's per-command timeout**, or is reported as its own `slot_busy` duration when an outer command timeout necessarily bounds the whole invocation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A run that exceeds `timeoutPerCommand` is classified as a timeout/infrastructure result naming the configured timeout and elapsed seconds, with a stable notice code; it never reports `reason: unknown` with `failures: []`.
- [ ] A run that exits non-zero or is killed with no parsable failures is classified as an unparsed/infrastructure condition carrying the command, exit code/signal and bounded stdout/stderr tails (not an empty `failures` list presented as a code failure).
- [ ] A run that waits for a test slot reports the wait as its own duration, distinct from suite elapsed time, with a stable `slot_busy`-style code.
- [ ] Queue wait is excluded from the suite's per-command timeout budget (or reported separately where an outer timeout bounds the whole invocation), proven by a test that stubs a blocking slot acquisition.
- [ ] Classification is proven by gate-classification unit tests plus a simulated timeout/kill fixture; no ad-hoc suite invocations.
- [ ] `implement/SKILL.md` and the test skill reference document the new classification fields and how to read them.

## Constraints

- Do not widen or bypass the host test semaphore (no `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` change here).
- Cache correctness is untouched; this item changes reporting/classification only.
- Framework repo boundaries: changes land in the SorraAgents skills (`test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `implement/scripts/implement.py`).
- UK English throughout.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `run_suite` (timeout/notice handling), `_paced` (slot acquisition vs runner timeout), `_test_concurrency_slot`, notice codes.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_run_resolved_suite`, `_gate_failure_kind`, `phase_finish`, `_resolve_test_timeout`.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/SKILL.md`, test skill reference docs.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6** — requirements + evidence owner for this item (tce-main-street).

# plan/intake AC coverage review creates duplicate "Close coverage gap" children when covering children already exist

Discovered-from: **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6** (tce-main-street) — observed while running `/skill:plan`.

## Problem

`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py:apply_coverage_review` (`action: auto_close`) creates one child per *parent AC it judges uncovered*, with the AC text copied verbatim and the title `Close coverage gap: [ ] **ACn — …**`. On a parent whose six feature children each restate an AC in their own words, it judged **all five** ACs uncovered and created five thin `idea`-stage duplicates alongside the real children.

Observed on `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6`:

- Six properly-formed children existed (config+guard, docs, three AC-verification children, validation) before the review ran.
- `apply_coverage_review(..., target_stage='plan_complete')` returned `action: auto_close` and created `MS-0MVTEXGU6007Z48U`, `MS-0MVTEXH6F008DVJF`, `MS-0MVTEXHK8002E376`, `MS-0MVTEXHWT0074M3M`, `MS-0MVTEXI9G002ROD0` (AC1–AC5).
- A follow-up `run_coverage_review` then reported `coverage_pct: 100` — mapping each parent AC **only** to the newly created gap child, i.e. the review's own output became its evidence.
- Resolution taken: all five were closed as duplicates with a comment mapping each AC to its real covering child, and the parent recorded the outcome.

## Why it matters

- The review silently degrades a well-planned tree (6 children) into 11, half of them AC-text stubs with no key files, constraints or evidence requirement — the opposite of what the review is meant to enforce.
- The "coverage" metric measures lexical similarity between the parent AC text and child AC text, not whether the child actually discharges the AC, so a correctly reworded child scores as a gap.
- Closing the duplicates afterwards leaves the parent at `plan_complete` with the tool's mapping invalidated, so a later re-run is ambiguous (re-create the stubs, or report gaps?).

## Suggested direction

- Before creating a gap child, require a **semantic/structural** match — e.g. child AC coverage by the parent's AC identifier (`AC1`, `AC2`, …, tolerant of reworded text) or by an explicit `Covers: ACn` line in the child description — and skip creation when matched.
- Treat `parent AC -> child` mapping as evidence only when the child has a non-stub body (ACs + Key Files/evidence), and prefer reporting `stop` with the specific unmatched ACs over creating thin children.
- Make the post-`auto_close` mapping exclude the auto-created children themselves when reporting `coverage_pct` (no self-satisfying evidence).
- Cover the case with a test: parent with 5 ACs, 5 reworded covering children → `action: proceed`, no children created.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A parent whose ACs are all covered by existing children — including children that reword the AC text — yields `action: proceed` and creates **zero** children.
- [ ] Gap children are created only when no child declares or demonstrably discharges the AC; the created child still restates the AC verbatim (current behaviour preserved for genuine gaps).
- [ ] `coverage_pct` never counts a gap child created by the same review as coverage for its own AC.
- [ ] Unit test(s) cover: fully-covered-with-reworded-AC → proceed; genuinely uncovered AC → auto_close with exactly one child; idempotent re-run creates no duplicates.
- [ ] `plan`/`intake` SKILL.md text states how coverage is matched, so agents can declare coverage (`Covers: ACn`) instead of relying on wording.

## Key Files

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/shared/tree_coverage.py` — `run_coverage_review`, `apply_coverage_review`, AC extraction/matching.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/plan/SKILL.md`, `~/.pi/agent/skills/intake/SKILL.md` — the documented coverage step.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/shared/tests/` — coverage-review unit tests.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6** — the planning session where this was observed (children `MS-0MVTEVJBH003GE8W`, `MS-0MVTEVJRX005N0EA`, `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`, `MS-0MVTEVKOD002OKSO`, `MS-0MVTEVL4Z009LUUR`, `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1`).

# Add `implement.py cleanup <id>` action for post-finish worktree removal

Parent: **SA-0MVTE927L0017ND5** — *implement.py finish deletes a plain leaf session's cwd, breaking its post-finish steps*.

**Goal.** Give the plain leaf flow one deterministic, safe, idempotent way to remove its own worktree **after** the session has finished everything that needs bash.

## Context

`phase_finish` removes the worktree right after the dev push (Step 7, `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`). In the plain leaf flow the finishing process is a child of the agent session, whose cwd **is** the worktree, so the session keeps a deleted cwd and Pi's bash tool refuses every later command (evidence: **RISE-0MVPZ31UJ000BC33**, 8 × `Working directory does not exist`).

The parent's chosen direction is *option 1*: `finish --keep-worktree` defers removal (the flag comes from **SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR**, delivered by the sibling child), and the **session's own final bash command** removes the tree. This child delivers that final command as a reviewed action rather than a raw `git worktree remove`:

- a raw `git worktree remove` would bypass the safety gates (`cleanup_worktree_processes`, "never remove a dirty tree") and could silently discard uncommitted work;
- `_remove_worktree` already solves the "invoking process sits inside the tree" problem by chdir-ing itself out before removal (verified: `git worktree remove --force "$(pwd)"` run from inside a worktree succeeds and leaves the *parent shell* with a dead cwd — which is exactly why removal must be the session's last command);
- re-running must be harmless (interrupted workflows).

The action also doubles as the building block for the *option 2* cleanup pass if the producer prefers that later — no rework, only the `SKILL.md` final-step wording changes.

## Intended contract (assert this; do not design an alternative)

`python3 skill/implement/scripts/implement.py cleanup <work-item-id> [--json] [--worktree-path <path>]`

1. **Resolve** the worktree: `.implement_state.json` → `--worktree-path` → `_discover_worktree(<id>)`. None found → report `retained_no_worktree` and exit 0.
2. **Terminal gate**: unless the item status is `completed` or `in_review` (read via `wl show <id> --json`), retain and report `retained_non_terminal`. Never remove.
3. **Dirty gate**: `_worktree_has_uncommitted_changes(path)` (the same gate the driver uses) → retain and report `retained_dirty`. Never `--force` past it.
4. **Remove**: `cleanup_worktree_processes(path)` → `_remove_worktree(path, repo_root=<state.repo_root>)` → `remove_state(path)`.
5. **Already absent**: the directory is gone → `already_absent: true`, success, stale state file cleared (idempotent).
6. **Report** (JSON via `format_json_output`, plus human lines): `removed`, `path`, `already_absent`, `retained_dirty`, `retained_non_terminal`, `retained_no_worktree`, `removed_state`, `message`. A retained tree prints the exact inspection/remedy command. Retained is a reported outcome, not a crash; only unexpected errors exit non-zero.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC2 — Cleanup still happens deterministically.** Whichever option is chosen, a finished leaf item's worktree is removed by a named step within the same workflow run (session final action or cleanup pass), with the removal recorded in the finish/cleanup report — here asserted by a test that drives the new `cleanup` action for a terminal item with a clean worktree: `cleanup_worktree_processes` then `_remove_worktree` run exactly once for the resolved path, the state file is removed afterwards, and the report records `removed: true`, `path`, `removed_state: true`.
- [ ] **AC4 — Interruption safety.** An interrupted workflow leaves the worktree present and reported (never half-removed), and a repeat run is idempotent: removing an already-absent worktree is a reported no-op success (`already_absent: true`, `removed: false`, exit 0) that still clears a stale state file, and a second invocation returns an equivalent report.
- [ ] **AC3 — Consistency with the driven fix.** The mechanism reuses the deferral predicate/flag introduced by SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR (`IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE`, `--keep-worktree` / `IMPLEMENT_KEEP_WORKTREE`) rather than adding a third removal path: patched-boundary tests prove the action calls `_remove_worktree` and `cleanup_worktree_processes` and adds no new deletion mechanism (no `rm -rf`, no bare `shutil.rmtree`, no second `git worktree remove` call site).
- [ ] **Safety gates (supporting the parent's constraints).** A non-terminal item and a worktree where `_worktree_has_uncommitted_changes` returns true are both **retained** (zero `_remove_worktree` calls) and reported as `retained_non_terminal` / `retained_dirty` with an actionable remedy line; a worktree path resolving to the main checkout is never passed to `_remove_worktree`.
- [ ] **CLI surface and in-code contract.** `cleanup` is accepted by `parse_args` (`choices`), dispatched in `main()`, documented in `--help`, and `phase_cleanup`'s docstring states the ordering contract ("run as the session's **last** bash command; nothing that needs the worktree cwd may follow").
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing/validation criterion.** New tests plus the changed-scope suite pass via the test skill (`/skill:test`); tests are written first (TDD) so they are red before the implementation and green after it.

## Minimal implementation

1. `phase_cleanup(work_item_id, json_output, worktree_path=None) -> dict[str, Any]` next to `phase_abort`, using `StatusLifecycle`-free read-only `wl show` for the status gate.
2. Reuse `_discover_worktree`, `_worktree_has_uncommitted_changes`, `cleanup_worktree_processes`, `_remove_worktree`, `remove_state`.
3. `parse_args`: add `cleanup` to `action` choices; `main()`: dispatch `phase_cleanup`.
4. Tests: `skill/implement/tests/test_cleanup_worktree_action.py`, patched-boundary style of `test_finish_no_diff_status.py` (no real removals, no real `wl` store, no `/proc` scanning).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_cleanup`, `parse_args`, `main()`; reuses `_remove_worktree` / `cleanup_worktree_processes` / `_worktree_has_uncommitted_changes` / `remove_state`.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_cleanup_worktree_action.py` — new tests.

## Out of scope

- Bulk sweep of every terminal item's worktree (`cleanup --terminal`) — deliberately deferred; this action is the building block if the producer later prefers option 2.
- `hygiene_check.sh` rework, branch deletion, Pi-core bash-tool behaviour.
data.title: Add implement.py cleanup action for post-finish worktree removal

# Plain-flow finish deferral: keep the worktree, report it loudly, prove it with tests

Parent: **SA-0MVTE927L0017ND5** — *implement.py finish deletes a plain leaf session's cwd, breaking its post-finish steps*.

**Goal.** In the plain leaf flow the worktree must still exist when `implement.py finish` returns, and finish must say so loudly enough that the session always runs the follow-up cleanup.

## Context

The deferral mechanism itself is delivered by **SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR** (`IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1` for driven children, plus the explicit `finish --keep-worktree` / `IMPLEMENT_KEEP_WORKTREE=1` hatch). This child is the **non-driven half**: it pins the plain-leaf behaviour with tests, closes any plain-flow gap the sibling leaves (e.g. a deferral report field written only on the driven path), and adds the "retained worktree" surface that makes a forgotten cleanup self-healing.

Root cause (parent): `phase_finish` Step 7 removes the worktree while the *session* still has its cwd inside it; Pi's bash tool then refuses every command (`Working directory does not exist`), while absolute-path `read`/`write` keep working — the session degrades exactly when it must write its comment, render its report and verify the pushed commit (evidence: **RISE-0MVPZ31UJ000BC33**).

Constraints inherited from the parent and the sibling item:

- **Do not change the driven behaviour.** `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1` semantics, driver-side removal and the drive sweep stay exactly as the sibling item delivers them; existing driven tests must stay green.
- **No third removal path and no new predicate.** `--keep-worktree` / `IMPLEMENT_KEEP_WORKTREE` (and `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE`) are the only deferral inputs; removal itself stays `_remove_worktree` + `cleanup_worktree_processes`.
- **Deferral must not be silent**: report field, log line and a copy-pasteable follow-up command.
- **Nothing after Step 7 needs the worktree** (verified in the sibling item's research: parent-branch sync, terminal-status write/read-back and the completion comment all act on the main checkout), so deferring cannot break the rest of finish.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — No dead cwd after finish in the plain flow.** A plain leaf session can still run bash commands after `implement.py finish` returns (or the workflow guarantees nothing after finish needs bash — depending on the chosen option), verified by a test that drives `phase_finish` and asserts the session-visible worktree state: with boundaries patched and the session cwd inside the worktree, the worktree and `.implement_state.json` still exist after finish returns.
- [ ] **AC2 — Cleanup still happens deterministically.** Whichever option is chosen, a finished leaf item's worktree is removed by a named step within the same workflow run (session final action or cleanup pass), with the removal recorded in the finish/cleanup report: `steps.worktree_removal == {"deferred": true, "reason": ..., "path": ...}`, the human and JSON output name the retained path with the exact `implement.py cleanup <work-item-id>` follow-up command (also added to the completion comment), and finish still reaches its terminal state (`completed` / `in_review`, push landed, status read-back passes).
- [ ] **AC3 — Consistency with the driven fix.** The mechanism reuses the deferral predicate/flag introduced by SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR (`IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE`, `--keep-worktree` / `IMPLEMENT_KEEP_WORKTREE`) rather than adding a third removal path: no new environment variable and no `/proc`-based holder detection, and without those flags `phase_finish` still runs `cleanup_worktree_processes` + `_remove_worktree`, reporting `worktree_removed: true` (the regression pin that keeps the sibling item's AC2 assertions green).
- [ ] **AC4 — Interruption safety.** An interrupted workflow leaves the worktree present and reported (never half-removed), and a repeat run is idempotent: re-running `phase_finish` on a retained worktree duplicates no state, `phase_start` resumes on the retained worktree instead of failing on `git worktree add`, and a subsequent `implement.py cleanup <id>` (child 1) removes it.
- [ ] **Driven behaviour untouched.** `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1` semantics, driver-side removal and the drive sweep stay exactly as SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR delivers them; `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py` passes unchanged.
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing/validation criterion.** New tests plus the changed-scope suite pass via the test skill (`/skill:test`); tests are written first (TDD).

## Minimal implementation

1. Pin the contract in a new `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_plain_flow_keep_worktree.py` (patched-boundary harness modelled on `test_finish_no_diff_status.py`).
2. Close any plain-flow gap in `phase_finish`: deferral report field + loud retained-path output/comment for the `--keep-worktree` path (the sibling owns the driven path).
3. Assert idempotence and `phase_start` resume-on-retained-worktree behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_plain_flow_keep_worktree.py` — new tests.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` (deferral report surface + retained-path output), `phase_start` (resume path, verification only).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py`, `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py` — patterns to follow and regressions to keep green.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR** — the `--keep-worktree` / `IMPLEMENT_KEEP_WORKTREE` hatch and the deferral predicate must exist before this item's tests can assert them.

# Document and wire the plain-flow ownership rule in the implement skill and docs

Parent: **SA-0MVTE927L0017ND5** — *implement.py finish deletes a plain leaf session's cwd, breaking its post-finish steps*.

**Goal.** Make the plain leaf flow carry one unambiguous, machine-checked ownership rule: `finish <id> --keep-worktree` defers removal, and the session's **last** bash command (`implement.py cleanup <id>`) removes the tree — with no competing `git worktree remove` instruction left anywhere.

## Context

The parent's research found **doc/instruction drift**: `skill/implement/SKILL.md` currently tells the agent to run `git worktree remove .worklog/worktrees/… && git worktree prune && git checkout dev && git pull` *after* pushing, while `phase_finish` Step 7 removes the worktree itself. In the plain leaf flow this drift is the bug: either the instruction is skipped (finish already removed the tree, killing the session's cwd) or it is attempted from a dead cwd.

This child lands after the two code children (child 1: `cleanup` action; child 2: plain-flow deferral + report surface), so every instruction it writes is runnable.

The rule to state, once, in three places:

- **Plain leaf flow** — `implement.py finish <id> --keep-worktree`; the session finishes its comment, report and post-push verification; then, as its **last** bash command, `implement.py cleanup <id>`. After that command no bash works in the session (the cwd is gone by design).
- **Driven child flow** — unchanged: the session never removes its own worktree; `implement.py drive` removes it after the session exits (**SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR**).
- **Parent/parent-phase flow** — unchanged: `phase_parent` finishes children in its own subprocess and removes their worktrees.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC5 — Documentation.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (finish step cleanup instructions), `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` and `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` state the ownership rule for the plain flow: who removes a worktree, in which flow (plain leaf / driven child / parent phase), in what order, and why the removal must come last.
- [ ] **AC2 — Cleanup still happens deterministically.** Whichever option is chosen, a finished leaf item's worktree is removed by a named step within the same workflow run (session final action or cleanup pass), with the removal recorded in the finish/cleanup report: `SKILL.md`'s finish step runs `implement.py finish <id> --keep-worktree`, and a new final step — explicitly the session's **last** bash command — runs `implement.py cleanup <id>` after the worklog comment, the end-of-session report and the post-push verification, including what to do when `cleanup` reports `retained_dirty` / `retained_non_terminal` (record it in a comment; never force).
- [ ] **AC3 — Consistency with the driven fix.** The mechanism reuses the deferral predicate/flag introduced by SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR (`IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE`, `--keep-worktree` / `IMPLEMENT_KEEP_WORKTREE`) rather than adding a third removal path: the docs state that `drive` removes driven children's worktrees after the session exits and that `phase_parent` keeps removal in finish, and the old competing manual `git worktree remove … && git worktree prune && git checkout dev` block is replaced so no instruction tells a session to remove a worktree it is standing in.
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.** Code comments/docstrings (`phase_finish`, `phase_cleanup`, `_remove_worktree`), `README.md`, `docs/dev/rca-main-checkout-wipe.md` and `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` are checked and corrected wherever they contradict the new rule.
- [ ] **Documentation is machine-checked.** Doc-contract tests (extending `tests/test_worktree_isolation_docs.py` and the existing `SKILL.md` doc-test pattern) assert the ownership text, the `--keep-worktree` finish command and the `cleanup` final step are present, and fail if the old competing `git worktree remove` instruction returns.
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing/validation criterion.** New tests plus the changed-scope suite pass via the test skill (`/skill:test`), and the dev-push full-suite gate is green for the pushed commit.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Minimal implementation

1. Rewrite the `SKILL.md` finish step: `--keep-worktree` on the finish command + a final "remove the worktree (last bash command)" step.
2. Add the ownership section to `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` and the contract paragraph to `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.
3. Extend `tests/test_worktree_isolation_docs.py` with the new contract assertions and the "old instruction must not return" negative assertion.
4. Sweep the remaining removal instructions named in AC4.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — finish-step cleanup instructions (currently the manual `git worktree remove` block) and the new final cleanup step.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — "Worktree removal ownership (plain leaf sessions)" section.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — ownership/ordering contract paragraph.
- `docs/dev/rca-main-checkout-wipe.md`, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — removal instructions to reconcile.
- `tests/test_worktree_isolation_docs.py` — doc-contract assertions.
- `README.md` — checked for finish/worktree claims that need updating.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by child 1** (`implement.py cleanup <id>` action) and **child 2** (plain-flow deferral + retained-path report surface) — the instructions must describe commands that exist.

## Goal

**As** a project owner scaffolding agent guidance from this repository, **I want** `templates/project-AGENTS.md` to carry the project-level conventions that audits actually enforce, **so that** a new project inherits the two rules that a 2026-10-29 cross-project audit session had to invent on the spot instead of discovering them late.

Discovered-from: `WL-0MVR8EXR6009F05V` (ContextHub) — an epic audit that returned `Ready to close: No` on an acceptance criterion the producer had already decided to accept, and an `implement` run whose push gate did not run the suite the skill documentation says it runs.

## Scope note (read before implementing)

The definite "the template" is taken to mean **`templates/project-AGENTS.md`** — the canonical project `AGENTS.md` seed consumed by `scripts/init_project_agents.py` (see `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md`). That file is deliberately minimal ("reference structure only"), so this item **adds project-level guidance sections, not a copy of the global rules**.

If the intent was instead the framework sources (`skill/audit`, `skill/report`, `skill/implement`) rather than the project template, re-scope this item before implementing — the framework findings are listed at the end as separate, unfiled work.

## Problem

Two conventions were needed during the ContextHub epic and neither is documented for a project owner:

1. **Recording a producer-accepted acceptance-criteria variance.** The producer decided to accept one AC without the last piece of live evidence. The audit runner ignores `wl auditWaiver` entirely (`grep -n waiver skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` → no matches); the *only* way to make an audit score that criterion `adjusted` (non-blocking) instead of `partial` (blocking) is to write the accepted variance into the criterion's own text in the work-item description, resolve the recorded open question, and *additionally* record `wl audit-waive` so the closure guard and `wl doctor audit-gaps` agree. Done that way, the epic audit returned `Ready to close: Yes` with the criterion `adjusted`, a clean Phase 1/Phase 2 (`calls=2 parse_ok=2`). Done any other way it silently stays blocking and the item ping-pongs between implement and audit.
2. **Declaring the project's real push gate.** `skill/implement` and `skill/audit` both state that the dev-push pre-push hook enforces the full suite (`run_tests.py --scope full`). That is true only where the v3 hook is installed: this repository ships `.githooks/pre-push` (v3, with the scope-aware test gate), but a project seeded earlier (ContextHub) still runs `worklog:pre-push-hook:v2`, which enforces branch policy, the context budget and worklog sync **and nothing else**. Green test evidence therefore came from the `implement.py finish` full-scope run, not the hook. A project owner needs to be told to assert this, because the failure mode is silent: pushes succeed and the cached full-suite evidence the audit consumes read-only never exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `templates/project-AGENTS.md` gains a `## Recording an accepted acceptance-criteria variance` section stating the three-step procedure — (a) amend the criterion's text in the work-item description with an explicit "Accepted variance (producer decision, <date>)" clause naming what evidence stands in for the missing evidence, (b) resolve the corresponding open question in the item description, (c) record `wl audit-waive <id> --reason "<why>"` — and explains **why** the description is mandatory (the audit runner scores an AC from its text and ignores `auditWaiver`).
- AC2: The same template gains a `## Declaring your push gate` section telling a project owner to verify which pre-push hook version the project actually runs (`git config core.hooksPath` + the `worklog:pre-push-hook:vN` banner line) and to record the answer in the project's own guidance, so the full-suite evidence an audit consumes is known to exist (or is known to come from `implement.py finish` instead of the hook).
- AC3: `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md` is updated to match — it must describe the template as carrying these two optional guidance sections and stay truthful about the "reference structure only, never a copy of the global rules" constraint; `scripts/init_project_agents.py` output must remain idempotent (re-running never duplicates the reference or the new sections).
- AC4: A test pins the guarantee: emitting a fresh project `AGENTS.md` via `scripts/init_project_agents.py` produces a file containing both new sections, and re-running it is a no-op (`scripts/init_project_agents.py --dry-run --json` reports no change).
- AC5: The two conventions stay project-scoped: no global workflow rule is duplicated into the template (the global layer remains `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` via `scripts/install_pi.sh`), and `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` is re-measured only if the template changes the always-loaded surface.
- AC6: Full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Key Files

- `templates/project-AGENTS.md` — the canonical project `AGENTS.md` seed; the two new sections go here.
- `scripts/init_project_agents.py` — the installer that reads the template (`TEMPLATE_PATH`) and must stay idempotent.
- `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md` — the installer documentation to keep in sync (it quotes the canonical file verbatim, so the quoted block must be updated too).
- `tests/` — wherever the installer's tests live (`grep -rln "init_project_agents" tests/`), for the AC4 pin.

## Constraints

- Do **not** copy global agent rules (workflow, wl lifecycle, coding disciplines) into the template — that duplication was removed by `SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G` and must not come back.
- Project-specific guidance stays project-specific: both new sections are conventions a *project owner* opts into, not new global mandates.
- Keep the installer idempotent and its output deterministic; no new dependency.
- UK English; match the existing Markdown style of the file and its quoted copy in the docs.

## Related findings from the same session (not in this item's scope — file separately if wanted)

1. `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` maps an AC verdict of `adjusted` to `unmet` in its Acceptance Criteria table (it only knows `met`/`unmet`), so a *passing* audit that carries an accepted variance renders as `❌ failed` with an `unmet` row. The report had to be corrected by hand.
2. `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py start` fails (`ERROR: Failed to create worktree …`) when a feature branch with the expected name still exists but its worktree directory was removed; the operator has to `git worktree add <path> <branch>` manually and re-run `start` (which then resumes idempotently).
3. `skill/audit` in-main-slot mode (default) emits `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` child screens that, when unserviced, produce a `Ready to close: No` whose AC rows are all `partial` **and** persist partial child audits that later block the parent — `--no-child-in-main-slot` was the only path that produced a usable report in three consecutive runs.

# implement.py start: nested node_modules symlink blocks submodule init (bootstrap ordering)

**Discovered from:** RISE-0MVRZKINX004HNEE (tce-the-rising implement run, 2026-10-29).

## Problem

`implement.py start` initialises submodules *after* it creates the
`node_modules` symlinks. When a submodule's own root has a `node_modules` in
the main checkout (tce-the-rising's `core` submodule does), the nested-symlink
pass creates `<worktree>/core/node_modules` inside the still-**empty**
submodule directory. `git submodule update --init` then cannot clone into
`core/` and fails:

```
fatal: clone of 'file:///home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine' into submodule path '…/core' failed
fatal: destination path '…/core' already exists and is not an empty directory.
```

Because submodule init failures are deliberately fail-open (SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ
AC2), `start` only logs a warning and the session proceeds with an
**uninitialised submodule**: `npm run build` (`tsc --noEmit`) then dies with
`Cannot find module './core/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin'`,
`@core-engine/SaveLoad`, etc. Every child session in that worktree must
hand-fix the checkout before it can build.

Secondary defect: even after a successful init, the symlink is not ignored by
the submodule's `.gitignore` (`node_modules/` has a trailing slash, which does
not match a *symlink*), so the superproject reports `M core` and the worktree
looks dirty.

## Evidence

- Call order in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (start phase):
  `_ensure_node_modules_symlink` (≈L4608) → `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`
  (≈L4614) → `_ensure_submodules` (≈L4618).
- Observed on tce-the-rising worktree
  `wl-RISE-0MVRZKINX004HNEE-…`: `git submodule status` showed
  `-19f30ac… core` (uninitialised) while `core/` contained only the
  `node_modules` symlink; the first `npm run build` produced ~40 `TS2307`
  errors from the missing submodule.
- Manual fix that worked: `rm core/node_modules && rmdir core`,
  `git -c protocol.file.allow=always submodule update --init --recursive`,
  re-create `core/node_modules`, and add `node_modules` to the submodule's
  `info/exclude` (the trailing-slash pattern in `core/.gitignore` does not
  match the symlink).

## Required change

- Run `_ensure_submodules` **before** the node_modules symlink passes, or make
  the nested-symlink pass skip paths that are inside an
  uninitialised/unchecked-out submodule (a gitlink with an empty directory).
- Make the worktree's `git status` clean after the symlinks are created: drop
  or neutralise the symlink's untracked status (e.g. immediately cover it by
  an exclude entry, or create the nested link only after init and add the
  path to the worktree's exclude).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A worktree whose submodule root has a `node_modules` in the main checkout is
  fully initialised by `start`: `git submodule status` in the worktree shows a
  checked-out submodule (no leading `-`) and the repo's build succeeds.
- Ordering regression test: fixture repo with a local-path submodule plus a
  `<submodule>/node_modules` in the main checkout → after `start`, the
  submodule is checked out at the recorded commit and the worktree
  `git status --porcelain` is clean.
- The fail-open contract is unchanged: a genuinely failing
  `git submodule update` still only logs a warning and does not abort `start`.
- No behavioural change for repos without submodules or without a submodule
  `node_modules`.
- `implement/SKILL.md` submodule section notes the ordering constraint.

## Constraints

- Do not remove the node_modules symlinking feature itself
  (SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B) — only fix its ordering/ignoring relative to
  submodules.
- Keep the change generic; no tce-the-rising / `core`-specific hardcoding.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_ensure_submodules`,
  `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`, start-phase call order.
- `skill/implement/tests/` — ordering/regression test next to
  `test_implement_submodules.py`-style fixtures.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — submodule documentation.
