## Problem statement

The ship skill's audit gates declare an `in_review` work item blocking while
reporting the reason `Ready to close` — a self-contradictory verdict — because
the content-fingerprint fast path silently never fires (the `check-freshness`
probe is invoked with an unsupported `--json` flag and its error is swallowed by
a fail-open `catch`), and in-gate remediation cannot restamp an audit that the
runner itself considers fresh. The result is a release that cannot proceed on a
passing audit with no actionable remedy short of a ~13-minute forced re-audit.

## Users

**Release operator** (runs `/skill:ship release` and reads the gate report):

> As a release operator, when every `in_review` item's audit content is
> unchanged since it was audited, I want the ship gates to treat that audit as
> current — no matter that `wl sync` moved `updatedAt` afterwards — so a release
> is never blocked by a passing audit whose only "staleness" is a timestamp.

> As a release operator reading a blocking report, I never want to see a
> blocking item whose reason says it passed; if the gate really must block, I
> want the reason to name the actual condition and give me a command that fixes
> it.

**Skill maintainer** (owns `skill/ship/scripts/`):

> As a maintainer, I want the gate→runner contract pinned by tests that assert
> the exact invocation shape, so a flag drift between `check-audit-gate.js` and
> `audit_runner.py` cannot silently degrade the fast path again.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **The content-freshness probe actually runs.** Either
   `audit_runner.py check-freshness <id> --json` is accepted by the runner's
   subparser (preferred: additive, matches the CLI already documented in
   `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and
   `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`), or the JS call sites stop
   passing `--json`. A unit test asserts the parsed-argument shape
   (`["check-freshness", "SA-1", "--json"]` parses, `command ==
   "check-freshness"`) **and** asserts the exact command string built by
   `queryContentFreshness()` stays in sync with it, so the two sides cannot
   drift apart again.
2. **A time-stale passing audit is upgraded by both gates.** A hermetic
   (injected-boundary) unit test proves that a `fresh: true` response
   turns a time-stale **passing** audit into a non-stale, non-blocking,
   non-remediated item in **both** `check-audit-gate.js`
   (`checkAuditReadyToClose`) and `check-final-validation.js`
   (`checkFinalValidation`) — including through the real
   `queryContentFreshness()` JSON parse, not only a stubbed
   `queryContentFreshnessFn`.
3. **No contradictory block after in-gate remediation.** A post-remediation
   status of `{passing: true, stale: true}` never produces `status:
   'blocking'` with reason `Ready to close`. The shared remediation path
   (`attemptAuditRemediation()`, used by the audit gate, the final-validation
   sweep and `refresh-audits.js`) re-queries content freshness and
   (a) returns `passing` with a reason naming the content-fresh basis when the
   fingerprint is unchanged, or (b) blocks with a reason that names the real
   condition (`time-stale but content changed`) plus the actionable remedy
   `audit_runner.py issue <id> --force`. An invariant test asserts no blocking
   entry is ever emitted with reason `Ready to close`.
4. **Regression test for the observed sequence.** A hermetic test reproduces
   the ContextHub failure exactly — audit `readyToClose: true`, `auditedAt` <
   `updatedAt`, v2 fingerprint present and unchanged, and a remediation
   `issue <id>` run that short-circuits (exits 0 leaving a passing but
   time-stale audit) — and asserts the gate does **not** block the release
   (item lands in `remediatedItems`/passes, exit status not 6/12).
5. **Docs state the contract.** `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`
   (where the content-fingerprint fast path is documented) and this repo's
   ship reference `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` both state that (i)
   content-fresh audits are trusted regardless of `updatedAt`, and (ii) an
   in-gate remediation that returns a passing-but-time-stale audit must not
   block. The `--json` flag for `check-freshness` is documented as supported.
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **No `--force` in the happy path.** The gate must not force a genuine
  re-audit (~13 min) merely because `updatedAt` moved; `--force` appears only
  as the documented remedy when content genuinely changed.
- **Preserve fail-open safety.** A probe failure must still fall back to the
  conservative time gate — never silently pass a stale audit.
- **Stay hermetic in tests.** No live `wl`/`audit_runner` invocations; reuse the
  existing injected boundaries (`runAuditShow`, `runAuditCommand`,
  `resolveAuditRunnerFn`, `queryContentFreshnessFn`, `createRemediationBudgetFn`).
- **One shared implementation.** The fix belongs in `attemptAuditRemediation()`
  / `queryContentFreshness()`, not duplicated in `check-final-validation.js`
  (Game-Scenes/Gym-Scenes parity principle: shared logic, not copies).
- **Do not weaken existing gates.** A genuine fresh failing verdict, a missing
  audit, or a content-changed audit must still block; `--skip-audit-remediation`
  semantics are unchanged.
- **Scope discipline.** The `audit_runner.py` `issue` short-circuit
  behaviour itself is out of scope (it is correct: it refuses to re-audit fresh
  content); record any further runner improvements as separate work items.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`
  - `queryContentFreshness()` (line ~442) builds
    `python3 "<runner>" check-freshness <id> --json` and swallows failures into
    `{fresh: false}`.
  - `checkAuditReadyToClose()` (line ~750) applies the fast path only when
    `status.stale && hasContentFingerprint(auditData)`, then remediates.
  - `attemptAuditRemediation()` (line ~643) runs `issue <id>` (no `--force`),
    re-reads `wl audit-show`, and blocks when
    `status.isBlocking || status.transient || status.stale` — this is where
    `{passing: true, stale: true}` becomes `blocking` with reason
    `Ready to close`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` mirrors the fast path
  (`classifyAudit`, ~line 630) and imports the shared
  `attemptAuditRemediation`/`queryContentFreshness`.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `check-freshness` subparser (line
  ~14933) accepts only `issue_id` and `--worklog-dir`; it always prints JSON.
  `cmd_issue` short-circuits a fresh audit (line ~10341) printing
  `Skipping: audit still fresh — Ready to close: Yes` and returning 0 without
  restamping `auditedAt`.
- Verified in this session: `audit_runner.py check-freshness <id> --json` →
  `error: unrecognized arguments: --json` (exit 2); without `--json` it prints
  the expected JSON (exit 0).
- Existing coverage does not catch either defect: JS tests inject
  `queryContentFreshnessFn` (bypassing the command string);
  `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py` parses
  `["check-freshness", "SA-1"]` without `--json`.

## Desired change

1. `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`: accept `--json` on the
   `check-freshness` subparser (output is already JSON), documented as accepted
   for compatibility with the ship gates.
2. `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`:
   - keep the command string and the runner parser in sync, pinned by tests;
   - extend `attemptAuditRemediation()` to accept an injectable
     `queryContentFreshnessFn`: when the post-remediation status is
     `passing && stale` **and** `hasContentFingerprint(auditData)`, probe
     content freshness — fresh → `status: 'passing'` with a content-fresh
     reason; not fresh/legacy/fingerprint-less → `status: 'blocking'` with
     reason naming `time-stale but content changed` and the
     `audit_runner.py issue <id> --force` remedy;
   - never emit a blocking entry whose reason is `Ready to close`.
3. `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js`: rely on the shared
   remediation fix (no duplicated logic); only adjust its report wording if
   needed for the new reason text.
4. Tests: extend `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`,
   `tests/unit/test-check-final-validation.mjs` (regression + invariant) and
   `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py` (`--json` parses).
5. Docs: update the contract paragraphs in
   `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and
   `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`; confirm `skill/ship/SKILL.md` Step-2
   wording still matches (it already claims the read-only probe runs).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — sync the probe command with the
  runner; teach `attemptAuditRemediation()` to resolve
  `passing + stale` by content freshness instead of blocking.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` — shared-remediation consumer;
  verify the fast path and post-remediation wording.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — accept `--json` on the
  `check-freshness` subparser.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py` — pin the accepted
  argument shape.
- `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` — command-shape, upgrade and
  regression/invariant tests.
- `tests/unit/test-check-final-validation.mjs` — mirrored fast-path and
  regression tests.
- `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — content-freshness contract
  (fast path + post-remediation).
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — mirrored contract statement.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — verify Step-2 wording matches the fixed behaviour.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — `check-freshness --json` now accurate.

## Related work

- **SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI** (completed) — introduced the content-fingerprint fast
  path this item repairs; its tests inject the probe so they never exercise the
  real command.
- **SA-0MUOO5UEB008RXBP** (completed) — shared staleness semantics between the
  Step-2 gate and the Step-3.7 sweep; the `passing: true, stale: true` state
  that produces the contradictory block comes from this sharing.
- **SA-0MVIDICGZ0030DXC** (completed) — `hasContentFingerprint()` v2-prefix
  detection (unchanged by this work).
- **SA-0MUOO5V0P00461X8** (completed) — bounded in-gate remediation; the
  contradiction is currently masked behind the budget logic.
- **SA-0MUOO5WV0006D7UD** (completed) — `--skip-audit-remediation`; that flag
  also blocks on this state, so the fix must reach it.
- **SA-0MUOO5TRU005ALBL**, **SA-0MUOO5VMH005VF69** (completed) — earlier
  stale-audit false-block elimination this item continues.
- **SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0** (completed) — item-data-only fingerprint semantics.
- Duplicate check: searched `audit gate freshness ship release` +
  `content fingerprint stale`; no completed item satisfies these ACs (all
  candidates predate and cause the defects) — this is a follow-up fix, not a
  duplicate.

### Related work (automated find-related report)

- **SA-0MRJBEJGY0095XAY** – Add recent-audit gate to audit skill startup
  (completed)
- **SA-0MSQJABHZ0018APE** – Content-gate child verdict reuse in parent audits
  (completed)
- **SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT** – Audit: content-based freshness gate (completed)

Repository file matches: `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`,
`docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (all confirm the
probe/contract locations named in **Key Files**).

## Related docs

- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` (Step 2 audit readiness gate)
- `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` (fast-path paragraph, line ~188)
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` (Step 2/3.7 gate descriptions)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (`check-freshness` read-only probe)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`_check_audit_freshness`,
  `cmd_check_freshness`)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** fixing the probe consistently may make the remediation path
  redundant for content-fresh items, so tests asserting "remediation attempted"
  counts will need updating. *Mitigation:* keep the existing budget/limit tests
  and add the new expectation alongside.
- **Risk:** a runner-side `--json` flag that is accepted-but-ignored could hide
  future output-format drift. *Mitigation:* pin the emitted JSON shape in the
  runner test and assert `queryContentFreshness()` parses it.
- **Risk:** reason-text changes break report-format tests. *Mitigation:* grep
  for `Ready to close` assertions before editing wording.
- **Risk (scope creep):** the audit runner's `issue` short-circuit and the
  remediation budget are tempting refactor targets. *Mitigation:* they are out
  of scope; file separate work items if improvements are spotted.
- **Assumption:** accepting `--json` in the runner is preferred over removing
  it from the JS, because four documentation locations and this repo's audit
  reference already document `check-freshness <id> --json` (additive, no
  doc-churn, and it hardens the CLI against exactly this class of drift).
- **Assumption:** updating both `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`
  and `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` is in scope, because existing tests
  (`tests/unit/test-ship-skill.mjs`) already assert these docs mirror each
  other on ship behaviour.
- **Assumption:** no producer decision is needed to proceed — the item body
  already fixes the root cause, ACs and preferred remedy direction.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Which side of the `--json` mismatch should be fixed — the runner or the
  JS call sites? — **Answer (Map, intake session, no producer answer required):**
  accept `--json` on the runner subparser. **Evidence:** `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`,
  `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and
  `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py` docstring already
  document `check-freshness <id> --json`; a live run confirms the flag is
  rejected (`unrecognized arguments: --json`, exit 2) while output is already
  JSON. Preferred option recorded; the alternative (strip `--json` from the JS)
  remains valid if the implementer prefers it, provided AC1's sync test exists.
- **Q:** May the gate block a passing-but-time-stale audit after remediation
  (AC2 option b), or must it always unblock (option a)? — **Answer (Map, intake
  session):** prefer (a) unblock when the content fingerprint is unchanged, and
  fall back to (b) only when content changed, since (a) removes the false block
  while (b) keeps genuine content-changed audits gated with an actionable
  `--force` remedy.
- **Q:** Is `refresh-audits.js` in scope? — **Answer (Map, intake session):** yes,
  implicitly — it consumes the shared `attemptAuditRemediation()`, so no
  separate changes are planned beyond keeping its tests green.
- **Q:** Should the audit runner's `issue` short-circuit be changed to restamp
  `auditedAt`? — **Answer (Map, intake session):** no. Restamping without a
  re-audit would falsify the audit timestamp; the gate must instead honour the
  runner's content-freshness verdict. Recorded as out of scope.

## Goal

As an agent running the changed-scope test gate, I want a changed `tests/unit/test-*.mjs` file to select the node suite for that directory, so a JS/TS test edit is actually executed before commit instead of only at the push-time full suite.

## Problem

`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_is_test_file()` recognises `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`, `*.test.mjs` and `*_test.mjs` but **not** the repo's dominant node convention `test-*.mjs`. Consequences:

1. A changed `tests/unit/test-*.mjs` file is not classified as a test file, so `map_changed_to_tests()` tries the convention mapping instead (`test_<stem>.py` etc.) and selects nothing.
2. The same filter builds the `all_tests` pool used by import-graph expansion, so `test-*.mjs` files can never be selected there either.
3. Emission of a node command requires a selected `.mjs` path, so no `node --test` command is produced at all.

Verified while delivering SA-0MVTU1WHS002HN1C: editing three test files (`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py`, `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`, `tests/unit/test-check-final-validation.mjs`) produced a changed-scope command containing only `pytest ...` — no `node --test`. 43 of the 44 `tests/unit/*.mjs` files use the `test-` prefix, so the gap covers almost the whole node unit suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `_is_test_file()` recognises `test-*.mjs` (and the equivalent `test-*.js`/`test-*.ts` naming already used by `tests/unit`) as test files.
- A unit test asserts that changing a `tests/unit/test-foo.mjs` file selects `tests/unit/test-foo.mjs` and causes a `node --test` command to be emitted by the changed-scope command builder (no pytest-only command).
- The selection never invents a path that does not exist (the existing LP-0MTZYRTNF0092JKW existence filter still applies).
- Existing changed-scope selection tests stay green; the full suite stays green.

## Constraints

- Do not widen selection to arbitrary `.mjs` helper files (e.g. `cli-helpers.mjs`); only the test-file naming conventions.
- Keep the single-source-of-truth rule: one filter function, no duplicated naming logic.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`
- `skill/test/tests/`

## Related work

- discovered-from:SA-0MVTU1WHS002HN1C (observed while adding hermetic ship-gate tests).

# Test harness: classification contract fixtures

Test-first slice for **SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z** (parent AC5; supplies the fixtures parent AC4 needs). These tests pin the contract and are **expected to fail (red)** until the runner and finish-gate slices land.

## Goal

Provide deterministic, simulated infrastructure-failure fixtures plus gate-classification unit tests, so a timeout, a kill and an unparsed non-zero exit are each provably distinguishable from a code failure — without any ad-hoc suite invocation and without real OOM or multi-minute sleeps.

## Scope

- Extend `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py` with fixture-driven cases: per-command `TimeoutExpired`, a signal-terminated child (`returncode < 0`), and a non-zero exit with no parsable failures.
- Extend `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_gate_failure_reason.py` with a classification case per new gate reason and per reported fact field.
- Add a small shared fixture helper (factory functions / stub command) that simulates each condition deterministically. Blocked slot acquisition is **stubbed**, never genuinely contended.
- Follow `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`: fixtures must exercise production classification code (**no Self-Referential Simulations**) and must not **Duplicate Existing Core Coverage** (the existing notice-code tests already cover slot_busy and command_not_found — extend, do not restate).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fixtures deterministically simulate (a) per-command timeout, (b) signal kill, (c) non-zero exit with unparsable output, and (d) blocked slot acquisition — with no real long sleeps and no host-slot contention.
- [ ] Tests assert the runner notice codes and fact fields (configured timeout, elapsed, exit code/signal, command, bounded tails) through production code paths.
- [ ] Classification is proven by gate-classification unit tests plus a simulated timeout/kill fixture covering timeout, kill, unparsed output and slot contention; no ad-hoc suite invocations.
- [ ] Tests assert the finish gate's reason for every condition never lands on `unknown` with an empty `failures` list.
- [ ] Every test asserts one behaviour with a meaningful failure message (no assertions on internal call counts that only mirror the implementation).

## Minimal implementation

1. Add a fixture helper module alongside the existing tests (factory functions returning fake `CompletedProcess`-shaped results and a stub semaphore/slot context manager).
2. Add runner-level tests that monkeypatch `_run_cmd` / the slot context rather than sleeping.
3. Add gate-level tests driving `_adapt_guarded_result` + `_gate_failure_kind` + `_gate_failure_message` with the new shapes.

**Key Files:**
- skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py
- skill/implement/tests/test_implement_gate_failure_reason.py
- skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md

## Constraints

- No `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` change; the host test semaphore is never widened or bypassed.
- Reporting/classification coverage only — cache correctness is untouched.
- UK English throughout.

## Deliverables

- Fixture helper + runner-level tests (timeout, kill, unparsed) in `skill/test/tests/`.
- Gate-level classification tests in `skill/implement/tests/`.
- A comment on this item recording the documented red run (which assertions fail and why).

## Dependencies

- None. This is the first slice; it blocks the runner slice.

# Runner: duration, timeout, kill and unparsed facts

First implementation slice of **SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z** (parent AC1, AC2, AC3, part of AC6). The runner emits facts; it does not decide what the agent should do with them.

## Goal

Make `run_tests.py` state, on every non-green suite result, exactly what happened — configured timeout vs elapsed execution time, a separate slot-queue wait, and the exit code/signal plus bounded output for unparsable failures — with stable machine-readable codes, so no consumer has to guess.

## Scope

- Add `elapsed_seconds` to every suite result (wall time of the **command execution only**) and aggregate `elapsed_seconds_total` in `run_all`.
- On `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`: keep `notice_code = suite_timeout` and add `configured_timeout` (the resolved `timeoutPerCommand`) plus `elapsed_seconds`.
- Signal-terminated child (`returncode < 0`): new stable `notice_code = killed` with `signal`, `exit_code`, `command` and bounded tails.
- Non-zero exit with no parsable failures: new stable `notice_code = unparsed_failure` with `exit_code`, `command` and bounded tails. This includes a non-zero result served **from cache** (elapsed unavailable — reported as null, never as `0`).
- Measure the slot-queue wait **once**, via the existing `paced_runner(on_wait=...)` callback, and report it as its own `slot_wait_seconds` field on the suite result and aggregated by `run_all`. Never fold it into `elapsed_seconds`.
- On `TestConcurrencyTimeout`, report `slot_wait_seconds` = the elapsed bounded wait.
- Precedence: structured parsable failures always win; the new codes apply only when `failures` is empty.
- Update `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` (failure-notice contract section) with the new fields and codes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A timed-out suite reports `notice_code = suite_timeout` with the configured timeout and elapsed seconds populated; `reason`-consuming callers can never see an unattributed timeout.
- [ ] A killed suite reports `notice_code = killed` with the signal, exit code, command and bounded stdout/stderr tails.
- [ ] A non-zero suite with no parsable failures (fresh or cache-served) reports `notice_code = unparsed_failure` with exit code, command and bounded tails.
- [ ] A slot wait is reported as `slot_wait_seconds`, distinct from `elapsed_seconds` (which excludes the wait), and `run_all` aggregates `notice_codes`, `elapsed_seconds_total` and `slot_wait_seconds` without dropping per-suite detail.
- [ ] `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` documents every new field and code with its unit/semantics.
- [ ] The parent's runner-level contract tests pass (changed-scope, via the test skill).

## Minimal implementation

1. Time the command execution with `time.monotonic()` around the subprocess call; carry it in each return path.
2. Thread an `on_wait`-measured `slot_wait_seconds` from the pacer/slot context into the result instead of adding a second timer.
3. Classify after the failure parser runs: structured failures → unchanged; else negative return code → `killed`; else non-zero → `unparsed_failure`.
4. Extend the aggregate loop in `run_all`.

**Key Files:**
- skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py
- skill/test_cache.py
- docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md

## Constraints

- No `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` change and no semaphore bypass.
- Cache keys and cache correctness untouched; cached failed results gain classification, not different storage.
- UK English throughout.

## Deliverables

- `run_tests.py` suite/aggregate results carrying `elapsed_seconds`, `configured_timeout`, `slot_wait_seconds`, and the `killed`/`unparsed_failure` notice codes.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` failure-notice contract updated.
- Green runner-level contract tests from the first slice.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by **SA-0MVU8XQTU006DP37** (test harness) — the contract tests land first.

# Finish gate: timeout, kill and unparsed reasons

Consumer slice of **SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z** (parent AC1, AC2, AC3, part of AC6). Depends on the runner slice: it classifies the facts the runner now emits.

## Goal

`implement.py finish` must tell the agent whether to fix code, raise `timeoutPerCommand`, or wait for a slot — by classifying timeout, kill, unparsed output and slot contention as distinct reasons, each carrying the facts that make the decision obvious.

## Scope

- Extend the gate-reason vocabulary in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: `timeout`, `killed`, `unparsed` alongside the existing `slot_contention`, `test_failure`, `infrastructure`.
- Map the runner's stable codes (`suite_timeout`, `killed`, `unparsed_failure`, `slot_busy`) to those reasons in `_gate_failure_kind`; an outer `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` around the gate run is also `timeout`. Structured failures keep precedence.
- `_gate_failure_message` renders the deciding facts: for `timeout` the configured timeout and elapsed seconds (plus the `timeoutPerCommand` headroom / wait-for-slot remedies); for `killed` and `unparsed` the command, exit code or signal and the bounded output tails.
- The `test_phase` report object carries `reason`, `configured_timeout`, `elapsed_seconds`, `slot_wait_seconds`, `command`, `exit_code` and `signal` when known.
- `_paced_runner` keeps the measured wait (from the existing `on_wait` callback) and surfaces it into the gate result instead of only logging it.
- `unknown` is retained only as a documented last resort, and only with a non-empty detail — never for a timed-out, killed or non-zero run.
- Update `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (gate-failure diagnostics section).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each of timeout, kill, unparsed output and slot contention yields a distinct `reason`, proven by gate-classification unit tests.
- [ ] A run that exceeds `timeoutPerCommand` is classified as a timeout/infrastructure result naming the configured timeout and elapsed seconds, with a stable notice code; it never reports `reason: unknown` with `failures: []`.
- [ ] A run that exits non-zero or is killed with no parsable failures is classified as an unparsed/infrastructure condition carrying the command, exit code/signal and bounded stdout/stderr tails (not an empty `failures` list presented as a code failure).
- [ ] `test_phase` carries `elapsed_seconds` and `slot_wait_seconds` as separate values, with the wait never added to the suite elapsed.
- [ ] Structured test failures still win classification (no genuine code failure is ever reported as infrastructure).
- [ ] `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` documents the new reasons and fields and how to read them.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add the three reason constants and extend `_gate_failure_kind` in code-first order (notice codes before legacy text prefixes).
2. Extend `_gate_failure_detail`/`_gate_failure_message` to render the fact fields per reason.
3. Populate the new `test_phase` keys where the report is built; keep the keys additive for existing consumers.

**Key Files:**
- skill/implement/scripts/implement.py
- skill/implement/tests/test_implement_gate_failure_reason.py
- docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md

## Constraints

- Reporting/classification only: no cache behaviour change, no semaphore widening.
- The finish gate stays changed-scope; the full suite remains the dev-push gate's job.
- UK English throughout.

## Deliverables

- New gate reasons (`timeout`, `killed`, `unparsed`) and fact fields in `implement.py`'s finish report and message.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` gate-diagnostics section updated.
- Green gate-classification tests from the first slice.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by **SA-0MVU8XRBQ000DG9D** (runner facts) — classification consumes the emitted codes and fields.

# Prove queue wait is outside the timeout budget

Verification slice of **SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z** (parent AC3, AC4). Depends on the runner and finish-gate slices.

## Goal

Prove, with a deterministic test, that time spent queued for a host test slot is neither charged to a suite's per-command timeout budget nor hidden inside the suite's elapsed time — and that it is reported as its own duration end to end.

## Scope

- Test that stubs a **blocking slot acquisition** (the slot context manager / semaphore acquire blocks for a controlled interval) and then runs a command whose own runtime plus timeout margin leaves no room for the wait: the command must still succeed, proving the wait was outside the timeout budget.
- Assert the wait is reported as `slot_wait_seconds` and that `elapsed_seconds` covers the command only (wait not folded in).
- Assert the same separation survives aggregation (`run_all`) and the finish-gate report (`test_phase`), including the bounded-wait expiry case where the whole wait duration is reported with the `slot_busy`-style code.
- Keep every interval small (seconds, not minutes) and keep the host semaphore out of it (stubbed acquisition, isolated `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` if a real semaphore is used).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test stubs a blocking slot acquisition and proves the per-command timeout budget is unaffected by the wait.
- [ ] The same test (or a sibling) proves `slot_wait_seconds` and `elapsed_seconds` are reported as separate values at suite, aggregate and finish-gate level.
- [ ] A run that waits for a test slot reports the wait as its own duration, distinct from suite elapsed time, with a stable `slot_busy`-style code, including the bounded-wait expiry path (so "waited then gave up" is distinguishable from "ran and failed").
- [ ] No real multi-minute sleep, no host-wide slot contention introduced by the test.
- [ ] Parent AC4 is covered by a named test referenced from the parent work item.

## Minimal implementation

1. Stub the slot context manager to sleep a controlled interval, recording entry/exit.
2. Run a fast stub command with a timeout just above its runtime; assert success and the reported fields.
3. Add the aggregate and gate-level assertions reusing the existing fixtures.

**Key Files:**
- skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_semaphore.py
- skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py
- skill/implement/tests/test_implement_gate_failure_reason.py

## Constraints

- No `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` change and no bypass of the host semaphore in production code (stubs live in tests only).
- UK English throughout.

## Deliverables

- Blocking-slot test proving wait is outside the per-command timeout budget.
- Suite/aggregate/gate assertions that `slot_wait_seconds` and `elapsed_seconds` are separate.
- Evidence comment on the parent work item naming the test that covers parent AC4.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by **SA-0MVU8XRTE008VDO2** (finish-gate reasons) — the gate-level assertions need the reported fields.

# Docs: classification fields in skill references

Documentation slice of **SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z** (parent AC6). Depends on the runner, finish-gate and queue-wait slices so the documented field names match the shipped code.

## Goal

An agent reading the implement and test skills must be able to interpret every finish-gate `reason` and its fact fields, and know the correct next action, without reading the source.

## Scope

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`: operator/agent-facing guidance on reading `reason` (`timeout`, `killed`, `unparsed`, `slot_contention`, `test_failure`, `infrastructure`) and the fact fields (`configured_timeout`, `elapsed_seconds`, `slot_wait_seconds`, `command`, `exit_code`, `signal`), including the correct remediation per reason (raise `timeoutPerCommand` with headroom / treat as infrastructure / inspect tails / wait a staggered delay).
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`: consistent wording and cross-references for the same codes/fields (no divergent names).
- Add a lightweight consistency check (docs-vs-source) so a renamed code cannot silently leave the docs stale.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `skill/implement/SKILL.md` documents each gate `reason`, the fact fields, and the recommended action for it.
- [ ] Both reference docs use the same code/field names as the source constants, with cross-references between them.
- [ ] A check (test or scripted grep with a clear failure message) fails when a documented code/field no longer exists in source, or a source code is undocumented.
- [ ] Content is UK English and consistent with the existing reference-doc structure.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add the classification table + remediation guidance to `skill/implement/SKILL.md`.
2. Align the two reference docs and cross-link them.
3. Add the consistency check next to the existing skill tests.

**Key Files:**
- skill/implement/SKILL.md
- docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md
- docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md

## Constraints

- Documentation and docs-consistency tooling only; no behaviour change.
- UK English throughout.

## Deliverables

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` classification/remediation guidance.
- Aligned `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` sections.
- Docs-vs-source consistency check.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by **SA-0MVU8XSGI003DBWR** (queue-wait proof) — documents the final field names and semantics.

# Tests: blocked-child classification matrix for `implement.py parent`/`drive`

Parent: **SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2** (*implement.py parent/drive start children whose status is blocked — re-validate the block before starting or skipping*).

**Test-first contract item.** Write these tests **before** the implementation
items C2 (`skip-blocked` via dep-edge re-validation), C3 (prose/cross-project
blockers) and C4 (`drive` propagation). They are expected to be **red** until
those land — they are the executable form of the parent's ACs 1–5.

## Goal

As an implement agent, I need an executable contract for how a child whose
`status` is `blocked` is classified, reported and (not) started, so that the
fix cannot silently regress and a stale block can never strand a child forever.

## Context (read before writing tests)

- `_classify_child()` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, ~line 1127)
  currently returns `skip-terminal` / `skipped-held` / `skip-in-progress` /
  `implement`. **`blocked` falls through to `implement`** — the defect.
- `phase_parent()` (~line 6609) populates `external_blockers` from outbound
  `wl dep` edges only and reports it as a coordination note; it never gates
  the start. `phase_drive()` (~line 7934) already re-propagates
  `blocked_children` from the parent report.
- The live failure: on 2026-10-29 `implement.py parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6`
  started child `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4` (status `blocked`, blocker in prose) and
  created a worktree; the child had to be aborted.
- Harness patterns to reuse: `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py`
  (`ParentHarness`, mocked `wl_show` / `wl_show_children` / `wl_dep_blockers` /
  `phase_start` / `_invoke_implement` / `_discover_worktree` /
  `StatusLifecycle.update_status` / `wl_add_comment` /
  `is_code_freeze_active`) and `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
  (`ScriptedParent` + `RecordingSpawner`).
- `wl show --children --json` already returns each child's `description` and
  `tags`, so prose blockers need no extra fetch; `wl dep list <id> --json`
  returns `outbound` entries carrying `id` and `status`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit tests cover: (a) `blocked` + open external blocker → not started, reported with ids; (b) `blocked` + blocker now terminal → stale block detected and child started; (c) `blocked` + no resolvable blocker → not started, message names the unresolved id; (d) `drive` propagates the same classification/report fields; (e) existing in-chain sibling ordering, cycles and terminal/in-progress behaviour unchanged (regression cases).
- [ ] New module `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` (pytest, module-scoped `implement_mod` fixture loading `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`; harness reused from `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py`, not re-implemented).
- [ ] **(a)** `blocked` child + **non-terminal** dep-edge blocker → child **not** started; its `children_processed` entry carries `action: "skip-blocked"` with `blocking_ids` naming the blocker, and is neither `skip-in-progress` nor `skipped-terminal`.
- [ ] **(b)** `blocked` child whose **every** dep-edge blocker is terminal (`completed` / `done` / `in_review`) or soft-deleted → **stale block** detected, child started, and the stale block is named in the report (e.g. `stale_blocks` / a message naming the blocker).
- [ ] **(c)** `blocked` child whose blocker is declared only in prose (a `**Blocked by (SorraAgents):** SA-…` line) with no dep edge and an id that cannot be resolved in this worklog → **not** started, and the report/message names that id together with where to check it (actionable, not silently ignored, not silently startable).
- [ ] **(d)** `phase_drive` propagates the same classification and blocker fields: no session is spawned for a `skip-blocked` child, and the drive report carries the child id plus its blocking ids (in `blocked_children` and/or the per-child entry).
- [ ] **(e)** Regression cases unchanged: in-chain sibling ordering (blocker implemented first), dependency cycle fail-fast (no child started, no status transition), terminal children never re-implemented, an `in_progress` child elsewhere is skipped and never clobbered, a soft-deleted sibling counts as terminal for in-chain gating.
- [ ] **Fail-closed case:** `blocked` child with **no** dep edges and **no** parseable `Blocked by` line → not started and reported as unvalidated (never defaults to startable).
- [ ] Update the superseded expectation in `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py::TestParentDependencyOrder::test_external_blocker_reported_not_started_early`: an out-of-chain blocker with no resolvable status must now **hold** the block (child reported `skip-blocked`, the startable sibling started) instead of the old "coordination note only, child started" behaviour. Rename the test so the new contract is obvious.
- [ ] Every test asserts a behaviour that production code (not a re-implementation) provides — no self-referential simulations (see `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`).
- [ ] Tests run through the test skill / finish gate (`/skill:test`), green together with the existing implement suites; never an ad-hoc runner. The full pytest + node suite is green at the dev-push gate (parent AC 8).

## Constraints

- Tests only — no production code in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` from this item.
- UK English throughout.
- Do not weaken or delete existing guards; the only expectation that changes is the superseded "external blocker is a coordination note only" case above.

**Key Files:**
- `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` — new test module (the matrix).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py` — harness pattern to reuse.
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — scripted-parent/recording-spawner harness for case (d).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py` — superseded external-blocker expectation to update.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — module under test (`_classify_child`, `phase_parent`, `phase_drive`).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2` — parent (blocked-child re-validation).
- `SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T` — introduced `external_blockers` as coordination notes; superseded by this work.
- `SA-0MVS1QS9J009DGPT` — the *parent's own* outbound edges / `blocked` status (adjacent, distinct code path; do not fold into this item).
- `SA-0MVO6UL70000HT0J` — terminal blockers still gate topological ordering (adjacent, distinct).

# `phase_parent`: classify a still-blocked child as `skip-blocked` (dep-edge re-validation)

Parent: **SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2**. Test-first sibling: **C1** (blocked-child classification matrix).

## Goal

As an implement agent running an epic, I need `implement.py parent` to never
start a child whose `status` is `blocked` while its block still holds, and to
re-evaluate (not honour forever) a **stale** block, so a verification child is
never implemented against a prerequisite that has not landed and a landed
prerequisite never strands its dependent.

## Context

- `_classify_child()` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, ~line 1127)
  returns `implement` for `status: blocked`. Precedence today:
  terminal → `skipped-held` → `skip-in-progress` → `implement`.
- `phase_parent()` (~line 6609) builds `classifications` with
  `action`/`external_blockers` and gates the start only on **in-chain**
  blockers (`_in_chain_blockers`, blockers that are themselves children of the
  same parent, ~line 6787). `_next_child_to_implement()` (~line 1227) is a
  second, legacy classification path kept consistent by tests.
- `wl dep list <id> --json` → `outbound` entries with `id` and `status`
  (`wl_dep_blockers`, ~line 565).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `blocked` child whose block still holds yields a **distinct** classification (`skip-blocked`, i.e. `ACTION_SKIP_BLOCKED`) from `_classify_child()` (or its caller); it is never `implement`, `skip-in-progress` or `skipped-terminal`. Precedence is explicit and documented: `skip-terminal` → `skipped-held` → `skip-in-progress` → `skip-blocked` → `implement`.
- [ ] **Dep-edge re-validation:** for a `blocked` child the outbound `wl dep list` edges are resolved; the block is **stale** iff every blocker is terminal (`completed`/`done`/`in_review`, reusing `_is_terminal_status` / soft-delete semantics) — in which case the child is startable again and the stale block is named in the report (a `stale_blocks` entry, and a log/comment line naming the blocker ids). Any **non-terminal** blocker holds the block.
- [ ] `children_processed` entries for a held child carry `action: "skip-blocked"`, the child id, its status and `blocking_ids` (the ids that hold it); the report also lists them in `blocked_children` so `phase_drive`'s existing propagation keeps working.
- [ ] A block that cannot be validated (no dep edges, no parseable blocker line, unknown status) is treated as **holding** and reported as unvalidated (`unvalidated_blocks`) — it must not default to startable. (The prose/cross-project resolution that makes such a child actionable lands in C3; until then the fail-closed behaviour is the correct default.)
- [ ] A `blocked` child with at least one terminal blocker **and** one non-terminal blocker still holds (the non-terminal one wins); a `blocked` child whose blockers are all soft-deleted is stale/startable.
- [ ] `_next_child_to_implement()` (legacy helper, still covered by `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py`) applies the same rule so the two classification paths cannot diverge; it is kept, not deleted.
- [ ] Unchanged: dependency order, cycle fail-fast, terminal children never re-implemented, `skipped-held` precedence, `skip-in-progress` never clobbering another agent's claim, `--finalise-stranded` semantics, and single-item `start`/`finish` behaviour.
- [ ] The C1 tests for cases (a), (b) and (e) are green; the changed-scope suite is green through the finish gate (`/skill:test`) and the full pytest + node suite is green at the dev-push gate (parent AC 8).

## Minimal implementation sketch

- Add `ACTION_SKIP_BLOCKED = "skip-blocked"` beside `ACTION_SKIPPED_HELD` (~line 213).
- New helper, e.g. `_blocked_child_state(child, blockers) -> {"action", "blocking_ids", "stale_ids", "unvalidated"}`, called from `_classify_child`'s callers (`phase_parent`, `_next_child_to_implement`) with the child's outbound edges — `_classify_child` itself has no edge data, so either widen its signature with an optional `blockers` argument (defaulting to `None` → unvalidated/fail-closed) or keep the status test in `_classify_child` and resolve the blocked verdict in the callers. Prefer the smallest change that keeps both call sites consistent.
- Extend the `classifications`/`child_results` entries and the "no startable child" message to name the blockers.

## Constraints

- Do not weaken existing guards; do not change `start`/`finish` single-item behaviour.
- Prefer declared dependency edges over prose; no `wl` schema change, no `gh`/network calls.
- UK English throughout.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_classify_child` (~1127), `_next_child_to_implement` (~1227), `phase_parent` (~6609, incl. `_in_chain_blockers` ~6787), `wl_dep_blockers` (~565), `TERMINAL_STATUSES`/`_is_terminal_status` (~1082).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` — C1's matrix (red to green).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py` — existing parent suite that must stay green.
- `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py` — existing dependency-order suite that must stay green.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2` — parent.
- `SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T` — introduced `external_blockers` as coordination notes (superseded here).
- `SA-0MVS1QS9J009DGPT` — the *parent's own* outbound edges / `blocked` status; distinct, do not implement here.

# Prose `Blocked by` and cross-project blockers hold a `blocked` child

Parent: **SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2**. Depends on **C2** (`skip-blocked` classification); test-first contract in **C1** (case (c)).

## Goal

As an implement agent, I need a blocker that is declared in the child's
description (the cross-project convention) to gate the start exactly like a
dependency edge, so a verification child is never started against an
unlanded prerequisite in another repository and the report tells me which id
to check and where.

## Context

- Cross-project blocks are written in prose, e.g. on
  `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`:
  `**Blocked by (SorraAgents):** \`SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2\` — *Finish gate: …* (in progress; …)`
  followed by an `**Unblock condition:**` line. `wl dep list` on that child
  returns `outbound: []`, so today the phase reports `external_blockers: []`
  and starts it.
- `wl show --children --json` already returns each child's `description`, so
  no extra fetch is needed to parse it.
- Ids in this worklog look like `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2` / `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1`;
  ids belonging to another repository's worklog are **not** resolvable from
  this one (`wl show` fails).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A narrowly scoped parser extracts blocker ids from an **explicit** `Blocked by …` line only (case-insensitive, tolerating the bold/labelled form `**Blocked by (SorraAgents):**` and a plain `Blocked by:`); it must not treat arbitrary prose, `Unblock condition:` text or `Related work` ids as blockers.
- [ ] **Re-validation of cross-project and prose blocks:** blocker IDs declared in the child description's `Blocked by …` line are collected and surfaced in `external_blockers` (id + resolvable status, or `unresolved`); an unresolvable cross-project id holds the block and is reported with an actionable message (id + where to check it), never silently ignored and never silently startable. The merged set gates the start via C2's `skip-blocked` verdict.
- [ ] **Resolvable** prose blocker (present in this worklog): terminal → stale (child startable, blocker named); non-terminal → holds, reported with its status.
- [ ] **Unresolvable** (cross-project / unknown) prose blocker → **holds**, and the report/message names the id plus where to check it (e.g. "check the owning project's worklog", with the id's prefix as the hint). Never silently ignored, never silently startable.
- [ ] A `blocked` child with **no** dep edges and **no** parseable `Blocked by` line is reported as **unvalidated** and holds (fail-closed) — never defaults to startable.
- [ ] Parsing never crashes the phase (fail-open on the parser, fail-closed on the verdict): a malformed line yields "unvalidated" rather than an exception.
- [ ] No `wl` schema change and no new machine-readable field: prose + declared dep edges only (the parent AC's "and/or a machine-readable `externalBlockers` field, whichever is implemented" is satisfied by this choice). Cross-project ids are not resolved over the network.
- [ ] C1 cases (c) and the fail-closed case are green; the changed-scope suite is green through the finish gate (`/skill:test`).

## Assumptions (recorded on the parent)

- A cross-project block can therefore never go stale automatically: when the
  external item lands, the child's owner must refresh the child (status
  `open`, or remove/annotate the `Blocked by` line). This is the fail-closed
  behaviour the parent's AC 3 asks for and is recorded as an assumption.

## Constraints

- Prose parsing must stay narrowly scoped (one explicit line); declared
  dependency edges remain the preferred mechanism.
- Do not weaken C2's fail-closed default, existing guards or single-item
  `start`/`finish` behaviour.
- UK English throughout.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — blocked-child state helper from C2, `phase_parent` classification/reporting (~6609), `wl_dep_blockers` (~565), `wl_show_children` (~525).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` — C1 matrix (case (c), fail-closed).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py` — existing parent suite that must stay green.
- `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py` — existing dependency-order suite that must stay green.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2` — parent.
- `SA-0MVS1QS9J009DGPT` — the *parent's own* outbound edges; distinct.
- `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` (tce-main-street) — origin epic whose `blocked` verification children use the prose convention; the live-evidence item `C6` exercises it.

# Regression tests pin the dev-push gate subject

Parent: **SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3** — test-first slice (written before the fix, in the
tracer-bullet `xfail(strict=True)` style already used by
`skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_commit_tree.py`).

## Goal

Pin the invariant *"the dev-push gate's subject is the pushed commit"* with
automated tests, so the code change in the sibling item is verified rather than
asserted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Retry push cwd is the worktree.** A regression test asserts the retry
  push's cwd/root is the worktree: driving `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` in
  a hermetic git sandbox records `git_push_to_dev` called with the **worktree**
  path (not `repo_root`) and with the **rebased** commit, so the hook's
  `--project-root` is the pushed tree.
- **First attempt cwd is the worktree.** A regression test asserts the first
  dev-push attempt also runs from the checkout that has the pushed commit
  checked out, so the main checkout's working tree is never the subject of the
  dev-push gate.
- **HEAD ≠ pushed sha cannot silently gate the wrong tree.** A test asserts the
  mismatch is either corrected or refused: the push is not attempted, and a
  fail-closed error names the commit, branch, worktree and the actual `HEAD`.
- **Gate evidence is surfaced on success.** A test asserts `git_push_to_dev()`
  logs the hook/push `stderr` on success (INFO/DEBUG) and that the logged
  evidence carries the gate's resolved tree — root path, `HEAD` sha, pushed sha
  and executed-vs-cached — so "the gate ran and hit a cache for commit X" is
  distinguishable from "the gate never ran". No wall-clock timing proxies: the
  classification is driven by cache entries set up in the fixture.
- **Hermetic.** Tests use `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` plus stubbed `wl`/store
  boundaries; they invoke no test command themselves and run no wall-clock
  sleeps.
- Tests carry a documented pre-fix baseline and fail before the fix, pass after
  it (markers removed in the fixing change set).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` — extend: retry push
  cwd/subject assertions (fixture already builds a hermetic sandbox + rebase).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_from_worktree.py` — new: first
  attempt cwd, subject guard, evidence logging/classification.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — factories only (no behaviour change).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Extend the existing recovery-test harness to record `git_push_to_dev` call
   args and the push cwd's `HEAD`.
2. New module: capture `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` and `phase_finish`
   Step-6 push args; assert cwd == worktree and pushed sha == worktree `HEAD`.
3. Assert the fail-closed message fields and the evidence record's fields via
   `caplog` (root, head, pushed, classification).
4. Mark the new expectations `xfail(strict=True)` until the sibling fix lands.

## Definition of Done

- The change-set gate (test skill) is green with the markers in place, and the
  new tests demonstrably fail when the pre-fix behaviour is restored.

## Dependencies / Deliverables

- No prerequisites. Blocks the implementation item (test-first ordering).
- Deliverable: failing-then-passing regression tests, no production code change.

# Push to dev from the worktree that holds the commit

Parent: **SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3** — the core fix (blocks nothing else, unblocks
the evidence and docs slices).

## Goal

`implement.py finish` must run its dev push from the checkout that has the
pushed commit checked out — the worktree — on the **first attempt and the
non-fast-forward retry**, so `.githooks/pre-push` resolves its
`--project-root` to the pushed tree. Fail closed when that tree cannot be
materialised.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Push cwd is the pushed tree.** `implement.py finish` runs its dev push from
  the checkout that has the pushed commit checked out (the worktree) — for the
  first attempt *and* the non-fast-forward retry — so the main checkout's
  working tree is never the subject of the dev-push gate.
- **Retry path re-establishes the subject.** After the recovery rebase rewrites
  the commit, the retry push has the rebased commit checked out (pushed sha ==
  push cwd `HEAD`), so the hook's `--project-root` is the pushed tree.
- **Fails closed with an actionable message.** A pre-push subject guard refuses
  the push when the push cwd does not hold the pushed commit (worktree gone,
  `HEAD` ≠ pushed sha, dirty state that cannot be rebased): finish raises an
  error naming the **commit, branch, worktree and the actual `HEAD`**, and
  never silently pushes from a checkout holding a different commit.
- **Recovery behaviour preserved.** Push timeout → process-group kill +
  recoverable-state comment; non-fast-forward → fetch + rebase + retry;
  worktree retained until the push succeeds. `_restore_local_dev_after_failed_push`
  and `_sync_parent_branch` still operate on the main checkout.
- **Step 5 stays hygiene only.** The local-dev fast-forward remains a main
  checkout hygiene step (never the gate subject); `repo_root` stays the subject
  of the main-checkout guard and of `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev`.
- **Cache compatibility preserved.** Full-suite evidence stays path-independent
  (`HEAD` sha + dirty-content hash + suite command): pushing from the worktree
  reuses/creates the same audit-acceptable `scope: full` entries, and
  `mirror_suite_cache` still mirrors the worktree cache into the main checkout.
- **Docs/comments in scope.** Code comments and docstrings that assert the old
  behaviour (the Step-5/Step-6 comments claiming the hook measures the main
  checkout, `git_push_to_dev`'s "cwd: worktree root" docstring) are corrected
  in this change set.
- **No weakening.** `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` and friends remain explicit escape
  hatches; the default path never fails open.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — phase_finish Step 6 push call site
  (currently `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, branch, commit_hash)`),
  `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` retry push, new subject guard +
  `PushSubjectMismatchError`, Step-5/Step-6 comments.
- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py`,
  `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_from_worktree.py` (markers
  removed here).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add `_assert_push_subject(push_cwd, commit_hash, branch, worktree_path)`:
   push cwd exists, is a git worktree, and `git -C push_cwd rev-parse HEAD`
   equals `commit_hash` — else raise `PushSubjectMismatchError` naming commit,
   branch, worktree and actual `HEAD`.
2. Step 6: guard, then `git_push_to_dev(worktree_path, branch, commit_hash)`.
   Keep the Step-5 fast-forward and the pre-push main-checkout guard on
   `repo_root`.
3. `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()`: after `git rebase origin/dev`, recompute
   `new_commit` **from the worktree**, guard, then retry
   `git_push_to_dev(worktree_path, branch, new_commit)`; keep the existing
   recoverable-state comments on failure.
4. Leave the ancestry assertion (Step 6a) reading `origin/dev` — it verifies
   what landed, not which cwd pushed.
5. Remove the `xfail(strict=True)` markers from the regression tests.

## Definition of Done

- Change-set tests green (retry cwd == worktree, first attempt cwd == worktree,
  guard refuses a mismatch), and a real `implement.py finish` dev push runs the
  full-suite gate with the worktree as `--project-root`.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (enforced at the
  dev-push gate on the pushed commit).

## Dependencies / Deliverables

- Prerequisite: the regression-test item (test-first ordering).
- Deliverable: `implement.py` push-from-worktree behaviour + guard + corrected
  comments.

# Surface dev-push gate evidence on success

Parent: **SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3** — observability slice; makes the gate auditable
and makes the 2026-10-28 68-second anomaly diagnosable.

## Goal

For every `implement.py finish`, make *"the gate ran and hit a cache for commit
X"* distinguishable from *"the gate never ran"* — without weakening the gate and
without executing tests from the pusher.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Gate evidence is surfaced.** Hook/push `stderr` is logged by
  `git_push_to_dev()` on success too (at least INFO/DEBUG) — today it is
  captured with `subprocess.PIPE` and logged only on failure.
- **Resolved tree visible in that output.** The logged evidence carries the
  gate's resolved tree: root path (the push cwd), the `HEAD` sha at that root,
  the pushed sha, and executed-vs-cached for the full-suite entry — so "the gate
  ran and hit a cache for commit X" is distinguishable from "the gate never
  ran".
- **Executed-vs-cached is derived from the test cache, not wall-clock.** Using
  the read-only `skill/test_cache.py` API for the pushed git state: no valid
  entry before the push + a valid entry after ⇒ `executed`; a valid entry
  already present before the push ⇒ `cached`; still no entry after a successful
  push ⇒ `no-evidence` (warned, and never silently reported as green).
- **Read-only, never weakening.** The evidence path executes no test command
  itself, does not alter the cache, keeps `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` and friends as
  explicit escape hatches, and never turns a gate-accepted push into a failure.
- **Machine-readable.** The classification is added to
  `report["steps"]["push"]` so `implement.py finish --json` exposes it.
- **Tests, no timing proxies.** A test covers the three classifications
  (`executed` / `cached` / `no-evidence`) by staging cache entries in the
  fixture and asserting the logged line via `caplog` — no wall-clock assertions.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev()` (stderr
  logging), phase_finish Step 6 reporting (`report["steps"]["push"]`).
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `compute_git_state()`, `query_cached()` (read-only
  calls only; no changes expected).
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` and/or
  `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_from_worktree.py` — classification
  tests.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Capture `stderr` on success and `LOG.info` it (keep `LOG.error` on failure).

   any) via `query_cached()`; after a successful push: re-query.
3. Emit one structured evidence line — e.g.
   `dev-push gate evidence: root=<cwd> head=<sha> pushed=<sha> full-suite=<executed|cached|no-evidence>`
   — and store the same dict under `report["steps"]["push"]["gate_evidence"]`.
4. Warn (not fail) on `no-evidence`, naming the commit, so a gate that did not
   run is visible without blocking recovery.

## Definition of Done

- Change-set tests green for all three classifications; a real finish over a
  cold cache logs `full-suite=executed`, over a warm cache `full-suite=cached`.

## Dependencies / Deliverables

- Prerequisite: the push-from-worktree item (the evidence must describe the
  pushed tree, which is the worktree).
- Deliverable: success-path hook logging + structured gate evidence in logs and
  `--json` output.

# test-failure: post-push ancestry assertion breaks 13 stub-based phase_finish tests

## Goal

As an implementing agent, I want the `skill/implement/tests/` group green on
`dev` again, so that the dev-push full-suite gate stops blocking every agent,
while the new post-push ancestry assertion keeps its real coverage.

## Root cause

Commit `d59ddcb7e` (SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U, child of the in-progress
SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY) added `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()`, called by
`phase_finish` after the push. It resolves the pushed commit and
`refs/remotes/origin/dev` with `git rev-parse --verify` via `run_cmd` and then
requires `git merge-base --is-ancestor`.

Thirteen existing `phase_finish` tests stub `implement.run_cmd` with a fake
that returns `returncode=0` and **empty stdout** for every git command. The
new assertion therefore resolves nothing, fails closed with
`AncestryAssertionError` ("refs/remotes/origin/dev (tip unresolved)") and makes
`finish` report failure — even where the test's subject is terminal-status
persistence, the main-checkout guard, the finish lock, repo-root resolution, or
the F1/F4 gate harnesses.

The same unresolved `rev-parse` makes `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push()`
refuse with `no_remote_tracking_ref`, so `own_churn` is empty and
`test_finish_own_fast_forward_churn_does_not_abort` aborts on finish's own
fast-forward churn. One test (`test_repo_root_resolution.py`) uses real git but
a stub commit hash (`abc1234`), so the commit cannot resolve there either.

## Failing tests (at 539b365d3)

- `test_finish_gate_commit_tree.py::test_baseline_capture_false_green_at_finish_gate_entry_point`
- `test_finish_gate_commit_tree.py::test_baseline_capture_parity_false_pass_from_a_foreign_cache_entry`
- `test_finish_gate_provenance.py::test_clean_change_set_runs_the_suite_exactly_once`
- `test_finish_gate_provenance.py::test_identical_tree_reuses_the_cached_verdict_without_spawning`
- `test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py::test_finish_own_fast_forward_churn_does_not_abort`
- `test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py::test_finish_clean_run_reports_guard_step`
- `test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py::test_finish_abort_before_worktree_removal_leaves_item_open`
- `test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py::test_finish_success_acquires_and_releases_lock`
- `test_finish_no_diff_status.py::test_finish_no_diff_path_persists_terminal_status`
- `test_finish_no_diff_status.py::test_finish_push_with_diff_path_persists_terminal_status`
- `test_finish_no_diff_status.py::test_finish_fails_loudly_when_terminal_status_missing_from_store`
- `test_finish_no_diff_status.py::test_finish_success_clears_assignee`
- `test_repo_root_resolution.py::test_finish_rejects_stale_state_repo_root_and_removes_worktree`

## Approach (test-only; no weakening)

- Fake-based harnesses: make each `_fake_run_cmd` model a **healthy, published**
  repository — a stable 40-hex commit for every `git rev-parse ...` — so the
  local-dev fast-forward and the post-push ancestry assertion both execute for
  real against the fake and pass. The assertion stays armed (it is not patched
  away).
- `test_repo_root_resolution.py` (real git + stub commit `abc1234`): stub the
  post-push ancestry boundary (`_assert_commit_on_origin_dev`) with a verified
  result, because the stub commit hash cannot exist in the fixture repository.
  The assertion's own behaviour is covered by
  `tests/test_implement_finish_local_dev_verified_sync.py`.
- No production change expected. If one is needed, it must not weaken
  fail-closed ancestry verification.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Group green:** `run_tests.py --group implement` passes at the pushed commit (all 13 previously failing tests pass; 0 failures).
- [ ] **Assertion stays exercised:** the fake `run_cmd` in the stub-based harnesses resolves `git rev-parse` to a commit and answers `merge-base --is-ancestor` success, so `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev` and `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push` run for real (no patch of the assertion in those files).
- [ ] **No weakening:** `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev` still fails closed when the commit/remote ref cannot be resolved; its dedicated tests remain green.
- [ ] **Dev-push gate:** the full suite is green on the pushed commit (pre-push gate) and `implement.py finish` reaches `completed`/`in_review`.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U** — introduced the ancestry assertion (`d59ddcb7e`).
- **SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY** — in-progress parent of that item.
- **SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2** — epic blocked by this red tree (discovered-from).
